1
邢巒李平
Xing Luan and Li Ping.
2
邢巒，字洪賓，河間鄚人也。 [1]五世祖嘏，石勒頻徵，不至。 嘏無子，巒高祖蓋，自旁宗入後。 蓋孫穎，字宗敬，以才學知名。 世祖時，與范陽盧玄、勃海高允等同時被徵。 後拜中書侍郎，假通直常侍、寧朔將軍、平城子，銜命使於劉義隆。 後以病還鄉里。 久之，世祖訪穎於羣臣曰：「往憶邢穎長者，有學義，宜侍講東宮，今其人安在？ 」司徒崔浩對曰：「穎臥疾在家。 」世祖遣太醫馳驛就療。 卒，贈冠軍將軍、定州刺史，諡曰康。 子脩年，即巒父也，州主簿。
Xing Luan, courtesy name Hongbin, came from Mo in Hejian commandery. [1] His fifth-generation ancestor Gu was summoned repeatedly by Shi Le but never answered the call. Gu had no son, so Luan's great-grandfather Gai was adopted into the line from a collateral branch of the clan. Gai's grandson Ying, courtesy name Zongjing, won fame for his learning and ability. Under Emperor Taiwu he was summoned to court together with Lu Xuan of Fanyang, Gao Yun of Bohai, and others. He was later made Vice Director of the Secretariat and, with acting rank as Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Pacifies the North, and Marquis of Pingcheng, carried an imperial commission to Liu Yilong's court. He later returned home on account of illness. Some time later Emperor Taiwu asked his ministers about Ying: "I still remember the elder Xing Ying—a man of learning and integrity who ought to lecture in the Eastern Palace. Where is he now? " Minister of Education Cui Hao answered, "Ying is bedridden at home. " The emperor dispatched the court physician by urgent relay to treat him. When he died he was posthumously honored as General Who Establishes Valor and Governor of Dingzhou, with the posthumous epithet Kang. His son Xiunian—Luan's father—served as chief clerk of the province.
3
巒少而好學，負帙尋師，家貧厲節，遂博覽書傳。 有文才幹略，美鬚髯，姿貌甚偉。 州郡表貢，拜中書博士，遷員外散騎侍郎，為高祖所知賞。 兼員外散騎常侍，使於蕭賾，還，拜通直郎，轉中書侍郎，甚見顧遇，常參座席。 高祖因行藥至司空府南，見巒宅，遣使謂巒曰：「朝行藥至此，見卿宅乃住，東望德館，情有依然。 」巒對曰：「陛下移構中京，方建無窮之業，臣意在與魏昇降，寧容不務永年之宅。 」高祖謂司空穆亮、僕射李沖曰：「巒之此言，其意不小。 」有司奏策秀、孝，詔曰：「秀、孝殊問，經權異策，邢巒才清，可令策秀。」
From boyhood Luan loved study; he carried his books from teacher to teacher, and though his household was poor he held fast to his principles until he had read widely in the classics and histories. He possessed literary talent and strategic sense, a fine beard, and a strikingly imposing bearing. Recommended by his province and commandery, he was appointed Erudite of the Secretariat, then promoted to Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and won the notice and esteem of Emperor Xiaowen. He also served as Supernumerary Regular Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary on a mission to Xiao Ze of Southern Qi. On his return he was made Attendant of Direct Communication and then Vice Director of the Secretariat, enjoyed exceptional favor, and was often present at the emperor's side. While taking his morning constitutional, Emperor Xiaowen came to the south of the Minister of Works' residence, saw Luan's home, and sent a messenger to say: "On my walk this morning I came this far, saw your house, and stopped. Gazing east toward your hall, the old feeling returns. " Luan replied, "Your Majesty has moved the capital to the central metropolis and is building an enterprise without end. My wish is to rise and fall with Wei—how could I trouble myself with a house meant to last forever?" " Emperor Xiaowen said to Minister of Works Mu Liang and Vice Director Li Chong, "In those words Luan's ambition is no small thing. " When the responsible offices reported on the examinations for the Cultivated Talent and Filial Piety categories, an edict read: "The Cultivated and the Filial call for different questions and different standards of judgment. Xing Luan's talent is outstanding—assign him the Cultivated examination."
4
後兼黃門郎。 從征漢北，巒在新野，後至。 高祖曰：「伯玉天迷其心，鬼惑其慮，守危邦，固逆主，乃至如此。 」巒曰：「新野既摧，眾城悉潰，唯有伯玉，不識危機，平殄之辰，事在旦夕。 」高祖曰：「至此以來，雖未擒滅，城隍已崩，想在不遠。 所以緩攻者，正待中書為露布耳。 」尋除正黃門、兼御史中尉、瀛州大中正，遷散騎常侍、兼尚書。
He later also served as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate. He accompanied the campaign north of the Han. Luan was at Xinye and arrived late. Emperor Xiaowen said, "Boyu's heart is lost to heaven and his counsel deluded by demons. He holds a doomed state yet clings to a rebellious master, and things have come to this pass. " Luan said, "Xinye is already destroyed and the other cities have all fallen. Only Boyu fails to see the danger. The hour of his complete destruction is only a matter of days. " Emperor Xiaowen said, "From this point on, though he has not yet been taken, his defenses are already broken. I think the end is near. The reason we are holding back the assault is simply to wait for the Secretariat to draft the victory proclamation." Soon afterward he was made Regular Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, concurrently Imperial Censor-in-Chief and Senior Rectifier of Yingzhou, then promoted to Regular Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and concurrent Director of the Secretariat.
5
世宗初，巒奏曰：「臣聞昔者明王之以德治天下，莫不重粟帛，輕金寶。 然粟帛安國育民之方，金玉是虛華損德之物。 故先皇深觀古今，去諸奢侈。 服御尚質，不貴雕鏤，所珍在素，不務奇綺，至乃以紙絹為帳扆，銅鐵為轡勒。 訓朝廷以節儉，示百姓以憂務，日夜孜孜，小大必慎。 輕賤珠璣，示其無設，府藏之金，裁給而已，更不買積以費國資。 逮景明之初，承升平之業，四疆清晏，遠邇來同，於是蕃貢繼路，商賈交入，諸所獻貿，倍多於常。 雖加以節約，猶歲損萬計，珍貨常有餘，國用恒不足。 若不裁其分限，便恐無以支歲。 自今非為要須者，請皆不受。 」世宗從之。 尋正尚書，常侍如故。
Early in Emperor Xuanwu's reign Luan memorialized: "I have heard that the enlightened kings of old who ruled the realm through virtue all prized grain and silk and held gold and jewels lightly. Grain and silk are what settle the state and nourish the people; gold and jade are mere vanity that erode moral character. Therefore the late emperor looked deeply into past and present and cast off every extravagance. He valued simplicity in dress and equipage, scorned carving and inlay, prized the plain over the ornate, and even used paper and silk for screens and copper and iron for bridle fittings. He taught the court frugality, showed the people his anxious concern for public affairs, and toiled day and night, careful in matters large and small. He held pearls and gems cheap to show he had no need of them. The gold in the treasury was only enough to meet immediate needs; he no longer bought and stockpiled it at the state's expense. By the opening of the Jingming era, inheriting an age of peace, the four borders were tranquil and subjects near and far were at one. Tribute missions lined the roads, merchants came and went, and the goods presented were more than twice the usual amount. Even with added restraint, the annual loss still ran to tens of thousands. Precious goods piled up while state funds were always short. Unless their allotments are cut back, I fear the treasury will not last the year. From now on, I ask that everything not truly necessary be refused." Emperor Xuanwu accepted his advice. He was soon made full Director of the Secretariat while retaining his post as Regular Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
6
蕭衍梁秦二州行事夏侯道遷以漢中內附，詔加巒使持節、都督征梁漢諸軍事、假鎮西將軍，進退徵攝，得以便宜從事。 巒至漢中，白馬已西猶未歸順，巒遣寧遠將軍楊舉、統軍楊眾愛、汜洪雅等領卒六千討之。 軍鋒所臨，賊皆款附，唯補谷戍主何法靜據城拒守。 舉等進師討之，[2]法靜奔潰，乘勝追奔至關城之下，蕭衍龍驤將軍關城流雜 〈疑〉 李侍叔逆以城降。 蕭衍輔國將軍任僧幼等三十餘將，率南安、廣長、東洛、大寒、武始、除口、平溪、桶谷諸郡之民七千餘戶，相繼而至。 蕭衍平西將軍李天賜、晉壽太守王景胤等擁眾七千，屯據石亭。 統軍韓多寶等率眾擊之，破天賜前軍趙䐗，擒斬一千三百。 遣統軍李義珍討晉壽，景胤宵遁，遂平之。 詔曰：「巒至彼，須有板官，以懷初附，高下品第，可依征義陽都督之格也。 」拜巒使持節、安西將軍、梁秦二州刺史。
When Xiao Yan's acting commissioner of Liang and Qin, Xiahou Daoyian, surrendered Hanzhong to Wei, an edict appointed Luan envoy bearing the staff, commander of all armies campaigning against Liang and Han, and acting General Who Pacifies the West, with full authority to advance, withdraw, levy troops, and act as circumstances required. When Luan reached Hanzhong, the region west of Baima had not yet submitted. He sent General Who Establishes Distance Yang Ju, army commander Yang Zhong'ai, Si Hongya, and others at the head of six thousand men to subdue it. Wherever the army's van went, the enemy submitted—only He Fajing, commander of the Bugu garrison, held his city and resisted. Ju and the others advanced to attack. [2] Fajing broke and fled. Pursuing in victory, they chased as far as Guancheng, where Xiao Yan's Dragon-Cavalry General Guancheng liu za Passage marked doubtful. Li Shishu thereupon surrendered the city. More than thirty of Xiao Yan's generals, including General Who Assists the State Ren Sengyou, led over seven thousand households from Nan'an, Guangchang, Dongluo, Dahan, Wushi, Chukou, Pingxi, Tonggu, and other commanderies to surrender in succession. Xiao Yan's General Who Pacifies the West Li Tianci, Administrator of Jinshou Wang Jingyin, and others gathered seven thousand men and encamped at Shiting. Army commander Han Duobao and others attacked them, routed Tianci's vanguard Zhao Zhe, and killed or captured thirteen hundred men. He sent army commander Li Yizhen against Jinshou. Jingyin fled by night and the place was pacified. An edict said: "When Luan arrives there he must appoint provisional officials to win over the newly submitted population. Ranks high and low may follow the standard used in the Yiyang campaign." Luan was appointed envoy bearing the staff, General Who Pacifies the West, and Governor of Liang and Qin provinces.
7
蕭衍巴西太守龐景民恃遠不降，巒遣巴州刺史嚴玄思往攻之，斬景民，巴西悉平。 蕭衍遣其冠軍將軍孔陵等率眾二萬，屯據深坑，冠軍將軍魯方達固南安，[3]冠軍將軍任僧褒、輔國將軍李畎戍石同。 巒統軍王足所在擊破之，梟衍輔國將軍樂保明、寧朔將軍李伯度、龍驤將軍李思賢，賊遂保回車柵。 足又進擊衍輔國將軍范峻，自餘斬獲殆將萬數。 孔陵等收集遺眾，奔保梓潼，足又破之，斬衍輔國將軍符伯度，其殺傷投溺者萬有餘人。 開地定民，東西七百，南北千里，獲郡十四、二部護軍及諸縣戍，遂逼涪城。 巒表曰：
Xiao Yan's Administrator of Baxi, Pang Jingmin, trusting in his distance from the capital, refused to submit. Luan sent Governor of Bazhou Yan Xuansi against him, executed Jingmin, and pacified all of Baxi. Xiao Yan sent his General Who Establishes the Host Kong Ling and others with twenty thousand men to hold Shenkeng. General Who Establishes the Host Lu Fangda fortified Nan'an, [3] while General Who Establishes the Host Ren Sengbao and General Who Assists the State Li Quan garrisoned Shitong. Wherever Luan's commander Wang Zu fought he broke the enemy, beheaded Xiao Yan's Generals Who Assists the State Yue Baoming, Who Pacifies the North Li Baidu, and Dragon-Cavalry Li Sixian, and the enemy fell back to the Huiche stockade. Zu advanced again against Xiao Yan's General Who Assists the State Fan Jun. All told, the killed and captured nearly reached ten thousand. Kong Ling gathered the survivors and fled to Zitong. Zu defeated them again and beheaded Xiao Yan's General Who Assists the State Fu Baidu. Those killed, wounded, or drowned exceeded ten thousand. They opened territory and settled the people across seven hundred li east to west and a thousand li north to south, took fourteen commanderies, two Protector-General districts, and numerous county garrisons, and pressed on to Fucheng. Luan memorialized:
8
揚州、成都相去萬里，陸途既絕，唯資水路。 蕭衍兄子淵藻，去年四月十三日發揚州，今歲四月四日至蜀。 水軍西上，非周年不達，外無軍援，一可圖也。 益州頃經劉季連反叛，鄧元起攻圍，資儲散盡，倉庫空竭，今猶未復，兼民人喪膽，無復固守之意，二可圖也。 蕭淵藻是裙屐少年，[4]未洽治務，及至益州，便戮鄧元起、[5]曹亮宗，臨戎斬將，則是駕馭失方。 范國惠津渠退敗，鎖執在獄。 今之所任，並非宿將重名，皆是左右少年而已，既不厭民望，多行殘暴，民心離解，三可圖也。 蜀之所恃唯劍閣，今既克南安，已奪其險，據彼界內，三分已一。 從南安向涪，方軌任意，前軍累破，後眾喪魂，四可圖也。 昔劉禪據一國之地，姜維為佐，鄧艾既出綿竹，彼即投降。 及苻堅之世，楊安、朱彤三月取漢中，四月至涪城，兵未及州，仲孫逃命。 桓溫西征，不旬月而平。 蜀地昔來恒多不守。 況淵藻是蕭衍兄子，骨肉至親，若其逃亡，當無死理。 脫軍克涪城，淵藻復何宜城中坐而受困？ 若其出鬬，庸蜀之卒唯便刀矟，弓箭至少，假有遙射，弗至傷人，五可圖也。
Yangzhou and Chengdu lie ten thousand li apart. The land route is cut off; they depend entirely on the waterways. Xiao Yan's nephew Yuanzao left Yangzhou on the thirteenth day of the fourth month last year and reached Shu on the fourth day of the fourth month this year. A fleet sailing west cannot arrive in less than a full year, and there is no outside military support. That is the first reason Shu can be taken. Yizhou has only lately endured Liu Jilian's rebellion and Deng Yuanqi's siege, which emptied its stores and granaries, and it has not yet recovered. The people have lost heart and no longer mean to hold out. That is the second reason. Xiao Yuanzao is a pampered young man [4] with no grasp of administration. As soon as he reached Yizhou he executed Deng Yuanqi [5] and Cao Liangzong. To kill generals on the eve of battle is to lose command of one's forces. Fan Guohui was defeated at the Jinqu Canal and is now shackled in prison. Those now in command are none of them seasoned generals of renown, only youthful favorites at court. They neither command popular respect nor refrain from cruelty, and the people's loyalty is breaking apart. That is the third reason. Shu relies on nothing but Jian'ge Pass. Now that Nan'an is taken, its strategic barrier is lost and a third of its territory within the border is already in our hands. From Nan'an to Fu the road lies open. The enemy vanguard has been broken again and again and the rear ranks have lost heart. That is the fourth reason. In the past Liu Shan held an entire kingdom with Jiang Wei as his chief aide, yet once Deng Ai emerged from Mianzhu they surrendered at once. Under Fu Jian, Yang An and Zhu Tong took Hanzhong in the third month and reached Fucheng in the fourth. The army had not yet reached the provincial capital when Zhongsun fled for his life. Huan Wen's western expedition pacified Shu in less than ten days. Shu has always been difficult to defend. Moreover Yuanzao is Xiao Yan's own nephew, his closest kin. If he flees, his uncle will surely have him put to death. If our army takes Fucheng, how can Yuanzao simply sit in the city and wait to be trapped? If he comes out to fight, the soldiers of Shu are handy only with blade and spear; they have very few bows and arrows, and even if they shoot from a distance they will hardly wound anyone. That is the fifth reason.
9
臣聞乘機而動，武之善經； 攻昧侮亡，春秋明義。 未有捨干戚而康時，不征伐而混一。 伏惟陛下纂武文之業，當必世之期，跨中州之饒，兼甲兵之盛，清蕩天區，在於今矣。 是以踐極之初，壽春馳款； 先歲命將，義陽克闢。 淮外謐以風清，荊沔於焉肅晏。 方欲偃甲息兵，候機而動，而天贊休明，時來斯速，雖欲靖戎，理不獲已。 至使道遷歸誠，漢境佇拔。 臣以不才，屬當戎寄，內省文吏，不以軍謀自許，指臨漢中，惟規保疆守界。 事屬艱途，東西寇竊，上憑國威，下仗將士，邊帥用命，頻有薄捷。 藉勢乘威，經度大劍，既克南安，據彼要險，前軍長邁，已至梓潼，新化之民，翻然懷惠，瞻望涪益，旦夕可屠。 正以兵少糧匱，未宜前出。 為爾稽緩，懼失民心，則更為寇。 今若不取，後圖便難，輒率愚管，庶幾殄克，如其無功，分受憲坐。 且益州殷實，戶餘十萬，比壽春、義陽三倍非匹，可乘可利，實在于茲。 若朝廷志存保民，未欲經略，臣之在此，便為無事，乞歸侍養，微展烏鳥。
I have heard that to strike when opportunity offers is the supreme principle of war; and to attack the benighted and despise a state in its death throes is the clear teaching of the Spring and Autumn Annals. Never yet has an age been pacified by laying aside arms, or the realm unified without campaigning. I humbly consider that Your Majesty continues the work of King Wu and King Wen, stands at the destined hour of assured succession, commands the wealth of the central provinces and the strength of armored hosts—to sweep the realm clean is a task for this very day. At the beginning of your reign Shouchun offered its allegiance; the year before last you sent generals forth and Yiyang was conquered. Beyond the Huai all was tranquil; along the Jing and Mian the borders grew calm. You had just wished to rest the armies and await the right moment, yet Heaven favors your glorious rule and the hour has come with such speed that, though you would prefer peace, necessity will not permit it. It has even brought Daoyian's surrender and Han territory waiting to be taken. I, lacking talent, have been entrusted with military command. Knowing myself to be a clerk at heart, I did not presume on military strategy; facing Hanzhong I intended only to secure the borders. The task proved arduous. Raiders struck east and west. Relying above on the state's majesty and below on officers and men, the frontier commanders obeyed orders and we won frequent minor victories. Riding our momentum we crossed the Great Sword Pass, took Nan'an, and held the strategic heights. The vanguard has marched far and reached Zitong. The newly submitted people have turned to us in goodwill. Fu and Yi lie before us and may fall at any moment. It is precisely because our troops are few and grain short that we ought not advance yet. Yet if we delay for that reason we risk losing the people's hearts, and they will turn to raiding again. If we do not take it now, later action will be far harder. I venture this humble counsel in hope of complete victory. If I fail, let me bear my share of punishment under the law. Moreover Yizhou is rich and populous, with more than a hundred thousand households—three times the prize of Shouchun or Yiyang. The gain to be seized lies here. If the court wishes only to protect the people and has no mind for conquest, then I have no further business here. I beg leave to return home and care for my parents, however briefly, in filial duty.
10
詔曰：「若賊敢闚𨵦，觀機翦撲； 如其無也，則安民保境，以悅邊心。 子蜀之舉，更聽後敕。 方將席卷岷蜀，電掃西南，何得辭以戀親，中途告退！ 宜勗令圖，務申高略。 」巒又表曰：
An edict replied: "If the enemy dares threaten the passes, watch for the moment and strike them down; if they do not, then settle the people and secure the borders to win the frontier's loyalty. Your campaign into Shu must await further orders. We are about to roll up Min and Shu and sweep the southwest like lightning—how can you plead devotion to your parents and withdraw midway! Press on with your plans and carry out the grand strategy." Luan memorialized again:
11
昔鄧艾、鍾會率十八萬眾，傾中國資給，裁得平蜀，所以然者，鬬實力故也。 況臣才絕古人，智勇又闕，復何宜請二萬之眾而希平蜀？ 所以敢者，正以據得要險，士民慕義，此往則易，彼來則難，任力而行，理有可克。 今王足前進，已逼涪城，脫得涪城，則益州便是成擒之物，但得之有早晚耳。 且梓潼已附，民戶數萬，朝廷豈得不守之也？ 若守也，直保境之兵則已一萬，臣今請二萬伍千，所增無幾。 又劍閣天險，古來所稱，張載銘云：「世亂則逆，世清斯順。 」此之一言，良可惜矣。 臣誠知征戎危事，不易可為，自軍度劍閣以來，鬢髮中白，憂慮戰懼，寧可一日為心。 所以勉強者，既得此地而自退不守，恐辜先皇之恩遇，負陛下之爵祿，是以孜孜，頻有陳請。 且臣之意算，正欲先圖涪城，以漸而進。 若克涪城，便是中分益州之地，斷水陸之衝，彼外無援軍，孤城自守，復何能持久哉！ 臣今欲使軍軍相次，聲勢連接，先作萬全之計，然後圖彼，得之則大克，不得則自全。
In the past Deng Ai and Zhong Hui led one hundred eighty thousand men and drained the central state's resources before they barely pacified Shu, because they fought with overwhelming force. How much less am I—whose talent falls far short of the ancients and whose wisdom and courage are wanting—fit to ask for twenty thousand men and hope to pacify Shu? I dare propose this because we hold the strategic passes and rugged ground, and gentry and people alike look to us for justice. It is easy for us to advance there and hard for them to come here; if we bring our strength to bear, victory is within reason. General Wang Zu has already advanced as far as Fucheng. Once Fucheng falls, Yizhou is as good as ours—it is only a question of whether we take it sooner or later. Zitong has already surrendered, with tens of thousands of households. How can the court leave it undefended? To hold it would take ten thousand men on the frontier alone. I am asking for only twenty-five thousand—a modest addition. Jian'ge, too, is nature's fortress, renowned since ancient times. As Zhang Zai's inscription puts it: "In chaotic times it turns hostile; in orderly times it opens itself. " That line alone is deeply lamentable. I know full well that war is perilous and not lightly undertaken. Since our troops crossed Jian'ge, my temples have gone half gray with worry and dread of battle—not for a single day have I been free of it. I press on only because to take this ground and then abandon it would betray the late emperor's kindness and Your Majesty's trust and pay. That is why I have kept at it and petitioned again and again. My plan is to take Fucheng first and advance step by step. Once Fucheng falls, we cut Yizhou in half and sever their land and water routes. Cut off from relief, how long can a lone citadel stand? I propose to march our forces in close succession, keeping our strength continuous. We must first secure every contingency, then strike. Success would mean a great conquest; failure would still leave us intact.
12
又巴西、南鄭相離一千四百，去州迢遞，恒多生動。 昔在南之日，以其統綰勢難，故增立巴州，鎮靜夷獠，梁州藉利，因而表罷。 彼土民望，嚴、蒲、何、楊，非唯五三，族落雖在山居，而多有豪右，文學箋啟，往往可觀，冠帶風流，亦為不少。 但以去州既遠，不能仕進，至於州綱，無由厠迹。 巴境民豪，便是無梁州之分，是以鬱怏，多生動靜。 比建議之始，[6]嚴玄思自號巴州刺史，克城以來，仍使行事。 巴西廣袤一千，戶餘四萬，若彼立州，鎮攝華獠，則大帖民情。 從墊江已還，不復勞征，自為國有。
Ba and Nanzheng lie fourteen hundred li apart from each other and far from the provincial seat—trouble flares there constantly. When we held the south, governance there was unwieldy, so Ba Province was established to pacify the tribal peoples. Liang Province profited from the arrangement and then petitioned to abolish it. The leading families of that region—the Yan, Pu, He, and Yang clans among many others—live in mountain settlements yet include numerous powerful magnates. Their literary petitions are often impressive, and cultured gentlemen are plentiful as well. Yet because they are so far from the capital, they cannot rise in office and have no path into provincial leadership. The local elites of Ba felt cut off from Liang Province, bred resentment, and stirred up trouble. When this plan was first raised, [6] Yan Xuansi proclaimed himself Prefect of Ba Province and has held power there ever since the city was taken. Ba spans a thousand li with more than forty thousand households. Establishing a province there to govern both Han settlers and tribal peoples would greatly placate the populace. From Dianjiang eastward, no further campaigns would be needed—the land would be securely ours.
13
世宗不從。 又王足於涪城輒還，遂不定蜀。
Emperor Xuanwu refused. Then Wang Zu withdrew suddenly from Fucheng, and the conquest of Shu was abandoned.
14
巒既克巴西，遣軍主李仲遷守之。 仲遷得蕭衍將張法養女，有美色，甚惑之。 散費兵儲，專心酒色，公事諮承，無能見者。 巒忿之切齒，仲遷懼，謀叛，城人斬其首，以城降衍將譙希遠，巴西遂沒。 武興氐楊集起等反叛，巒遣統軍傅豎眼討平之，語在豎眼傳。 巒之初至漢中，從容風雅，接豪右以禮，撫細民以惠。 歲餘之後，頗因百姓去就，誅滅齊民，藉為奴婢者二百餘口，兼商販聚歛，清論鄙之。 徵授度支尚書。
After Luan conquered Ba, he sent the garrison commander Li Zhongqian to hold it. Zhongqian took the daughter of Xiao Yan's general Zhang Fayang—a woman of striking beauty—and became utterly smitten. He squandered military supplies on wine and women, and no official business could reach him. Luan was furious. Zhongqian, fearing for his life, plotted rebellion, but the townspeople beheaded him and surrendered to Xiao Yan's general Qiao Xiyuan. Ba was lost. The Di chieftain Yang Jiqing of Wuxing and others rose in rebellion. Luan sent Commander Fu Shuyan to put them down; the full account appears in Shuyan's biography. When Luan first arrived in Hanzhong, he carried himself with easy grace, treated local elites with courtesy, and dealt kindly with the common people. After a year, he began executing ordinary families over questions of loyalty, enslaving more than two hundred people, and profiteering through trade. Men of reputation held him in contempt. He was recalled and appointed Minister of Revenue.
15
時蕭衍遣兵侵軼徐兗，緣邊鎮戍相繼陷沒，朝廷憂之，乃以巒為使持節、都督東討諸軍事、安東將軍，尚書如故。 世宗勞遣巒於東堂曰：「蕭衍寇邊，旬朔滋甚，諸軍舛互，規致連戍陷沒。 宋魯之民尤罹湯炭。 誠知將軍旋京未久，膝下難違，然東南之寄，非將軍莫可。 將軍其勉建殊績，以稱朕懷，自古忠臣亦非無孝也。 」巒對曰：「賊雖送死連城，犬羊眾盛，然逆順理殊，滅當無遠。 況臣仗陛下之神算，奉律以摧之，平殄之期可指辰而待，願陛下勿以東南為慮。 」世宗曰：「漢祖有云『金吾擊郾，吾無憂矣』，今將軍董戎，朕何慮哉。」
When Xiao Yan's forces raided Xu and Yan and frontier garrisons fell in succession, the court grew alarmed and appointed Luan Bearer of the Staff, Commander of Eastern Expeditionary Forces, and General Who Pacifies the East, while retaining his post as minister. At the Eastern Hall, Emperor Xuanwu bid Luan farewell with these words: "Xiao Yan ravages our borders day by day. Our armies clash with one another and our garrisons fall one after another. The people of Song and Lu suffer most cruelly. I know you have only lately returned to the capital and find it hard to leave your parents, yet the southeast has no one else to trust but you. Strive for outstanding achievement to meet my expectations. Loyal ministers have never lacked filial devotion. " Luan replied, "Though the rebels hold city after city and their numbers are great as a flock of beasts, the righteous and the rebellious stand on opposite grounds—their destruction cannot be far off. And with Your Majesty's wise guidance and proper discipline, their annihilation is near at hand. I beg Your Majesty not to worry about the southeast. " Emperor Xuanwu said, "When Han the Founder's forces struck Ying, he said he had no further worries. With you commanding our armies, what have I to fear?"
16
先是，蕭衍輔國將軍蕭及先率眾二萬，寇陷固城； 冠軍將軍魯顯文、驍騎將軍相文玉等率眾一萬，屯於孤山； [7]衍將角念等率眾一萬，擾亂龜蒙，土民從逆，十室而五。 巒遣統軍樊魯討文玉，別將元恒攻固城，統軍畢祖朽討角念。 樊魯大破文玉等，追奔八十餘里，斬首四千餘級。 元恒又破固城，畢祖朽復破念等，兗州悉平。 巒破賊將藍懷恭於睢口，進圍宿豫。 而懷恭等復於清南造城，[8]規斷水陸之路。 巒身率諸軍，自水南而進，遣平南將軍楊大眼從北逼之，統軍劉思祖等夾水造筏，燒其船舫。 眾軍齊進，拔柵填塹，登其城。 火起中流，四面俱擊，仍陷賊城，俘斬數萬。 在陳別斬懷恭，擒其列侯、列將、直閤、直後三十餘人，俘斬一萬。 宿豫既平，蕭昞亦於淮陽退走，二戍獲米四十餘萬石。
Earlier, Xiao Yan's general Xiao Jixian had led twenty thousand men and captured Gucheng; Champion General Lu Xianwen and Valiant Cavalry General Xiang Wenyu encamped ten thousand men on Lone Mountain; [7] Xiao Yan's general Jiao Nian and others led ten thousand men to ravage the Gui and Meng region, where half the local households joined the rebellion. Luan sent Commander Fan Lu against Wenyu, Yuan Heng against Gucheng, and Commander Bi Zuxiu against Jiao Nian. Fan Lu routed Wenyu's forces, pursued them eighty li, and took more than four thousand heads. Yuan Heng retook Gucheng, Bi Zuxiu defeated Jiao Nian, and Yan Province was fully pacified. Luan defeated the rebel general Lan Huaigong at Suikou and marched to besiege Suyu. Huaigong then built a fortress at Qingnan, [8] aiming to sever our land and water lines of communication. Luan personally led his forces south across the water while General Yang Dayan pressed from the north. Liu Sizu and others built rafts on both banks and burned the enemy fleet. The armies advanced together, tore down palisades, filled the moats, and stormed the walls. Fires blazed on the water as attacks converged from every side. The rebel fortress fell, with tens of thousands killed or captured. In battle they beheaded Huaigong and captured more than thirty of his nobles, generals, and staff officers, killing or capturing ten thousand men. With Suyu pacified, Xiao Bing withdrew from Huaiyang as well. The two garrisons yielded more than four hundred thousand shi of grain.
17
世宗賜巒璽書曰：「知大龕醜虜，威振賊庭，淮外霧披，徐方卷壒，王略遠恢，混一維始，公私慶泰，何快如之！ 賊衍此舉，實為傾國。 比者宿豫陷歿，淮陽嬰城，凶狡侜張，規抗王旅。 將軍忠規協著，火烈霜摧，電動岱陰，風掃沂嶧，遂令逋誅之寇，一朝殲夷； 元鯨大憝，千里折首。 殊勳茂捷，自古莫二。 但揚區未安，餘燼宜盪，乘勝掎角，勢不可遺。 便可率厲三軍，因時經略，申威東南，清彼江介，忘此仍勞，用圖永逸，進退規度，委之高算。 」又詔巒曰：「淮陽、宿豫雖已清復，梁城之賊，猶敢聚結，事宜乘勝，并勢摧殄。 可率二萬之眾渡淮，與征南掎角，以圖進取之計。」
Emperor Xuanwu sent Luan an imperial letter: "You have crushed the enemy's stronghold and shaken their court. Beyond the Huai the fog has lifted; in Xu the dust of war settles. Our royal design reaches far and unification begins—what greater joy for throne and people alike! This campaign of the rebel Xiao Yan truly risked his entire state. Recently Suyu had fallen and Huaiyang had held out, while the enemy's cunning leaders schemed to resist the imperial forces. Through your steadfast counsel and coordinated action—fierce as fire, swift as frost, lightning at the foot of Mount Tai, wind sweeping through Yi and Yi—you annihilated these long-elusive rebels in a single morning; the great whale of villainy beheaded a thousand li away. Such extraordinary merit and brilliant victory are unmatched since antiquity. Yet the Yang region is not secure, and lingering embers must be stamped out. You must press the advantage in concert—this momentum cannot be squandered. Lead the three armies, exploit the moment, extend our power into the southeast, and clear the Yangtze frontier. Accept present hardship for lasting peace. As for the conduct of the campaign, I leave all to your judgment. " A further edict read: "Though Huaiyang and Suyu are restored, the rebels at Liangcheng still gather. Strike while victory is fresh and destroy them with combined force. Cross the Huai with twenty thousand men and coordinate with the southern expeditionary force to press the advance."
18
及梁城賊走，中山王英乘勝攻鍾離，又詔巒帥眾會之。 巒表曰：「奉被詔旨，令臣濟淮與征南掎角，乘勝長驅，實是其會。 但愚懷所量，竊有未盡。 夫圖南因於積風，伐國在於資給，用兵治戎，須先計校。 非可抑為必勝，[9]幸其無能。 若欲掠地誅民，必應萬勝； 如欲攻城取邑，未見其果。 得之則所益未幾，不獲則虧損必大。 蕭衍傾竭江東，為今歲之舉，疲兵喪眾，大敗而還，君臣失計，取笑天下。 雖野戰非人敵，守城足有餘，今雖攻之，未易可克。 又廣陵懸遠，去江四十里，鍾離、淮陰介在淮外，假其歸順而來，猶恐無糧艱守，況加攻討，勞兵士乎？ 且征南軍士從戎二時，疲弊死病，量可知已。 雖有乘勝之資，懼無遠用之力。 若臣之愚見，謂宜修復舊戍，牢實邊方，息養中州，擬之後舉。 又江東之釁，不患久無，畜力待機，謂為勝計。 」詔曰：「濟淮掎角，事如前敕，何容猶爾磐桓，方有此請！ 可速進軍，經略之宜聽征南至要。」
When the Liangcheng rebels fled, Prince Ying of Zhongshan pressed the attack on Zhongli, and Luan was ordered to bring his forces to join him. Luan memorialized: "I have received Your Majesty's order to cross the Huai and coordinate with the southern expedition, riding our victory in a long advance—a true opportunity. Yet my humble judgment still harbors reservations. Flight to the south depends on steady wind; conquest depends on supply. War demands careful reckoning beforehand. One cannot assume certain victory [9] and count on the enemy's incompetence. To ravage the countryside and slaughter the people, one must be utterly assured of victory; to assault cities and seize towns, I see no promise of success. Success would bring little gain; failure would bring great loss. Xiao Yan poured all of Jiangdong into this year's campaign, only to return with exhausted armies and heavy losses—a failure that has made him and his court a laughingstock. They may be weak in the field, but they can defend cities well enough. An assault now would not be easily won. Guangling lies far away, forty li from the Yangtze; Zhongli and Huaiyin stand beyond the Huai. Even if they surrendered willingly, holding them without adequate grain would be hard—how much harder to take them by force and wear out our troops? The southern expeditionary forces have campaigned for two seasons; their exhaustion, sickness, and death are plain to see. We may have the momentum of victory, but I fear we lack the strength for a distant campaign. In my humble view, we should repair the old garrisons, strengthen the frontier, let the heartland recover, and plan a later offensive. Trouble from Jiangdong will surely come again. To husband our strength and await the right moment is the wiser strategy. " The edict replied: "Cross the Huai and coordinate as previously ordered. How dare you still hesitate and petition thus! Advance at once. As for operational details, defer to the southern expeditionary commander."
19
巒又表曰：「蕭衍侵境，久勞王師，今者奔走，實除邊患，斯由靈贊皇魏，天敗寇豎，非臣等弱劣所能克勝。 若臣之愚見，今正宜修復邊鎮，俟之後動。 且蕭衍尚在，凶身未除，螳蜋之志，何能自息。 唯應廣備以待其來，實不宜勞師遠入，自取疲困。 今中山進軍鍾離，實所未解，若能為得失之計，不顧萬全，直襲廣陵，入其內地，出其不備，或未可知。 正欲屯兵，蕭密餘軍猶自在彼； [10]欲言無糧，運船復至。 而欲以八十日糧圖城者，臣未之前聞。 且廣陵、任城可為前戒，豈容今者復欲同之。 今若往也，彼牢城自守，不與人戰，城壍水深，非可填塞，空坐至春，則士自弊苦。 遣臣赴彼，糧何以致？ 夏來之兵，不齎冬服，脫遇冰雪，取濟何方？ 臣寧荷怯懦不進之責，不受敗損空行之罪。 鍾離天險，朝貴所具，若有內應，則所不知，如其無也，必無克狀。 若其不復，其辱如何！ 若信臣言也，願賜臣停； 若謂臣難行求回，臣所領兵統悉付中山，任其處分，臣求單騎隨逐東西。 且俗諺云，耕則問田奴，絹則問織婢。 臣雖不武，忝備征將，前宜可否，頗實知之，臣既謂難，何容強遣。 」詔曰：「安東頻請罷軍，遲回未往，阻異戎規，殊乖至望。 士馬既殷，無容停積，宜務神速，東西齊契，乘勝掃殄，以赴機會。 」巒累表求還，世宗許之。 英果敗退，時人伏其識略。
Luan memorialized again: "Xiao Yan's invasion long taxed the imperial armies. His flight has truly lifted the border threat—but this victory came through divine favor for Great Wei and heaven's judgment on the rebels, not through any merit of ours. In my view, we should now repair the frontier garrisons and wait for a better opportunity. Xiao Yan yet lives and his evil is unabated. A mantis's ambition does not die of its own accord. We should fortify our defenses and await his next move—not wear ourselves out on a distant expedition. I do not understand the advance on Zhongli. If one weighed costs against gains, abandoned every safeguard, and struck straight at Guangling deep in enemy territory by surprise—perhaps that might at least make some sense. Just when we would need to encamp, Xiao Mi's remaining forces are still in the field; [10] when we claim they lack grain, supply ships arrive. To besiege a city on eighty days' rations—I have never heard of such a thing. Guangling and Rencheng should serve as warning enough. How can we repeat the same mistake? If we go, they will shut themselves in fortress walls and refuse battle. Deep moats cannot be filled. We would sit idle until spring while our men sicken and weary. If I am sent there, how will grain reach us? Summer troops carry no winter gear. If we meet ice and snow, where shall we find relief? I would rather accept blame for cowardice than bear guilt for a doomed march ending in defeat. Zhongli is a natural fortress—the court officials know this well. If there is inside help, I cannot say; without it, capture is impossible. If we fail to take it, the disgrace will be unbearable! If Your Majesty credits my words, I beg permission to halt. If you deem me unwilling and seeking retreat, I will transfer all my troops to Prince Zhongshan for his disposition. I ask only to follow the campaign on horseback alone. As the proverb says: ask the field hand about plowing, the weaver about silk. I am no warrior, yet I am a campaign general and know what is feasible. Having said this is impossible, how can I be forced to go? " The edict replied: "The General Who Pacifies the East repeatedly asks to stand down, dallies without advancing, and obstructs the military plan—far from what we expect. Our forces are ready and must not lie idle. Move swiftly, coordinate east and west, ride the victory to annihilate the enemy, and seize the moment." Luan petitioned repeatedly to withdraw, and Emperor Xuanwu consented. Prince Ying was indeed defeated and driven back, and contemporaries admired Luan's foresight.
20
初，侍中盧昶與巒不平，昶與元暉俱世宗所寵，御史中尉崔亮，昶之黨也。 昶、暉令亮糾巒，事成許言於世宗以亮為侍中。 亮於是奏劾巒在漢中掠良人為奴婢。 巒懼為昶等所陷，乃以漢中所得巴西太守龐景民女化生等二十餘口與暉。 化生等數人，奇色也，暉大悅，乃背昶為巒言於世宗云：「巒新有大功，已經赦宥，不宜方為此獄也。 」世宗納之。 高肇以巒有克敵之效，而為昶等所排，助巒申釋，故得不坐。
Earlier, Attendant-in-Ordinary Lu Chang and Luan were at odds. Both Chang and Yuan Hui enjoyed Emperor Xuanwu's favor, and Imperial Censor-in-Chief Cui Liang belonged to Chang's faction. Chang and Hui set Liang on Luan's trail, promising that if the case succeeded they would recommend Liang to Emperor Xuanwu for appointment as Attendant-in-Ordinary. Liang then memorialized the throne, accusing Luan of seizing innocent people in Hanzhong and reducing them to bondage. Fearing entrapment by Chang and his allies, Luan sent Hui more than twenty captives taken in Hanzhong, among them Huasheng, daughter of Pang Jingmin, governor of Baxi. Huasheng and several of the women were of rare beauty. Hui was delighted, broke with Chang, and pleaded Luan's cause before Emperor Xuanwu: "Luan has just won a great victory and already received pardon. It is unseemly to reopen this prosecution now. " Emperor Xuanwu agreed. Gao Zhao, seeing that Luan had defeated the enemy yet was being squeezed out by Chang's faction, helped clear him, and so Luan escaped punishment.
21
豫州城民白早生殺刺史司馬悅，以城南入，蕭衍遣其冠軍將軍齊苟仁率眾入據懸瓠。 詔巒持節率羽林精騎以討之。 封平舒縣開國伯，食邑五百戶，賞宿豫之功也。 世宗臨東堂，勞遣巒曰：「司馬悅不慎重門之戒，智不足以謀身，匪直喪元隸豎，[11]乃大虧王略。 懸瓠密邇近畿，東南藩捍，度公之在彼，[12]憂慮尤深。 早生理不獨立，必遠引吳楚，士民同惡，勢或交兵。 卿文昭武烈，朝之南仲，故令卿星言電邁，出其不意。 卿言早生走也守也？ 何時可以平之？ 」巒對曰：「早生非有深謀大智能構成此也，但因司馬悅虐於百姓，乘眾怒而為之，民為凶威所懾，不得已而苟附。 假蕭衍軍入應，水路不通，糧運不繼，亦成擒耳，不能為害也。 早生得衍軍之接，溺於利欲之情，必守而不走。 今王師若臨，士民必翻然歸順。 圍之窮城，奔走路絕，不度此年，必傳首京師。 願陛下不足垂慮。 」世宗笑曰：「卿言何其壯哉！ 深會朕遣卿之意。 知卿親老，頻勞於外，然忠孝不俱，才宜救世，不得辭也。」
Bai Zaosheng, a townsman of Yuzhou, killed Governor Sima Yue and opened the southern quarter of the city. Xiao Yan sent his Champion General Qi Gouren to lead troops in and seize Xuanhu. An edict appointed Luan Bearer of the Staff and ordered him to lead elite Feathered Forest cavalry against the rebels. He was enfeoffed as Founding Marquis of Pingshu with a fief of five hundred households, a reward for his victory at Suyu. Emperor Xuanwu received Luan at the Eastern Hall and sent him forth with these words: "Sima Yue ignored every warning at his own gate. He lacked the wit to save himself—not only did he lose his head to a lackey, [11] he dealt a grave blow to our royal strategy. Xuanhu presses close upon the capital and shields the southeast frontier. Knowing you will be there, [12] my anxiety runs especially deep. Zaosheng cannot stand on his own; he is sure to call in aid from Wu and Chu. Officials and commoners alike hate him, and the fighting may spread. You unite civil brilliance with martial valor—the court's own pillar of the south. Go swift as starlight and lightning, and take them unawares. Tell me: will Zaosheng flee or stand his ground? How soon can the rebellion be crushed? " Luan answered: "Zaosheng has neither deep design nor great talent to have built this rebellion. He merely rode the people's fury after Sima Yue's cruelty. The common folk, cowed by his violence, joined him because they had no choice. Even if Xiao Yan's troops came to his aid, with the waterways blocked and supplies cut off they would be taken too and could do no lasting harm. Once Zaosheng has Liang reinforcements in hand, greed will hold him fast—he will defend the city and not run. When our armies arrive, officials and people alike will turn back to us at once. Pen him in his exhausted city, cut off every escape, and before the year is out his head will reach the capital. Your Majesty need give the matter no further thought. " Emperor Xuanwu smiled. "What bold words! You understand exactly why I am sending you. I know your parents are aged and that you are worn from repeated campaigns abroad, yet loyalty and filial piety cannot both be fully served, and talent such as yours is meant to save the age. You may not refuse."
22
於是巒率騎八百，倍道兼行，五日次於鮑口。 賊遣大將軍胡孝智率眾七千，去城二百，逆來拒戰。 巒擊破孝智，乘勝長驅，至於懸瓠。 賊出城逆戰，又大破之，因即渡汝。 既而大兵繼至，遂長圍之。 詔加巒使持節、假鎮南將軍、都督南討諸軍事。 征南將軍、中山王英南討三關，亦次於懸瓠，以後軍未至，前寇稍多，憚不敢進，乃與巒分兵掎角攻之。 衍將齊苟仁等二十一人開門出降，即斬早生等同惡數十人。 豫州平，巒振旅還京師。 世宗臨東堂勞之，曰：「卿役不踰時，克清妖醜，鴻勳碩美，可謂無愧古人。 」巒對曰：「此自陛下聖略威靈，英等將士之力，臣何功之有。 」世宗笑曰：「卿匪直一月三捷，所足稱奇，乃存士伯，欲功成而不處。」
Luan then led eight hundred horsemen at forced march, halting at Baokou on the fifth day. The rebels dispatched Grand General Hu Xiaozhi with seven thousand men to meet him two hundred li from the city. Luan routed Xiaozhi, pressed the pursuit, and drove straight to Xuanhu. When the rebels sallied out to fight, he broke them again and at once crossed the Ru. The main force soon arrived, and he laid a tight siege. An edict promoted Luan to Bearer of the Staff, Acting General Who Pacifies the South, and Commander of All Southern Expeditionary Forces. Prince Ying of Zhongshan, General Who Campaigns South, was also campaigning south against the Three Passes and halted at Xuanhu. His rear guard had not yet come up and the enemy ahead were growing numerous; afraid to advance, he joined Luan in a pincer assault. Qi Gouren and twenty-one other Liang officers opened the gates and surrendered. Luan at once executed Zaosheng and several dozen of his accomplices. With Yuzhou pacified, Luan led his troops home in good order to the capital. Emperor Xuanwu received him at the Eastern Hall and praised him: "You finished the campaign without delay, crushed the rebel rabble, and won merit grand enough to face the ancients without shame. " Luan replied, "This was Your Majesty's sage strategy and imperial majesty, and the work of Prince Ying and his officers and men. What merit is mine? " Emperor Xuanwu smiled. "Your three victories in a single month are wonder enough—but you also have the true knight's grace: winning glory yet refusing to claim it."
23
巒自宿豫大捷，及平懸瓠，志行修正，不復以財賄為懷，戎資軍實絲毫無犯。 遷殿中尚書，加撫軍將軍。 延昌三年，暴疾卒，年五十一。 巒才兼文武，朝野瞻望，上下悼惜之。 詔賻帛四百匹，朝服一襲，贈車騎大將軍、瀛州刺史。 初，世宗欲贈冀州，黃門甄琛以巒前曾劾己，乃云：「瀛州巒之本邦，人情所欲。 」乃從之。 及琛為詔，乃云「優贈車騎將軍、瀛州刺史」，議者笑琛淺薄。 諡曰文定。
After his great victory at Suyu and the pacification of Xuanhu, Luan straightened his conduct. He no longer sought bribes and never touched military funds or supplies. He was made Director of the Palace Secretariat with the additional rank of General Who Pacifies the Army. In the third year of Yanchang he died suddenly of illness at fifty-one. Luan united civil and military gifts, and court and country alike looked to him. High and low mourned his loss. The throne granted four hundred bolts of burial cloth and one set of court robes, and posthumously made him General of Chariots and Cavalry and governor of Yingzhou. At first Emperor Xuanwu had wished to grant Jizhou posthumously. But Huangmen Zhen Chen, whom Luan had once impeached, argued: "Yingzhou is Luan's native commandery—the place custom would choose. " The emperor assented. When Chen drafted the edict, he wrote only "honor him as General of Chariots and Cavalry and governor of Yingzhou," omitting the grand general's title. Observers mocked his pettiness. His posthumous name was Wending.
24
子遜，字子言。 貌雖陋短，頗有風氣。 解褐司徒行參軍。 襲爵。 後遷國子博士、本州中正。 因謁靈太后，自陳：「功名之子，久抱沉屈。 臣父屢為大將，而臣身無軍功階級，臣父唯為忠臣，不為慈父。 」靈太后慨然，以遜為長兼吏部郎中。 出為安遠將軍、平州刺史。 時北蕃多難，稽留不進，免。 孝莊初，除輔國將軍、通直散騎常侍、東道軍司，討逆賊劉舉於濮陽，不克。 還，除散騎常侍，加前將軍。 永安二年，坐受任元顥，除名。 尋除撫軍將軍、金紫光祿大夫。 出帝時，轉衞將軍、右光祿大夫。 孝靜初，以本官領嘗藥典御，加車騎將軍。 久之，除大司農卿，與少卿馬慶哲至相糾訟。 遜銳於財利，議者鄙之。 武定四年卒，年五十六。 贈本將軍、光祿勳卿、幽州刺史。
His son Sun, courtesy name Ziyan. Plain and short in appearance, he nevertheless carried himself well. On entering office he became a staff adjutant in the chancellor's service. He inherited the marquisate. He was later made erudite of the Imperial University and rectifier of his native prefecture. On audience with Empress Dowager Ling he declared: "As the son of a man of great merit, I have long languished in obscurity. My father served repeatedly as a great general, yet I hold no military rank at all. He was a loyal minister to the throne—but no loving father to me." " Moved, Empress Dowager Ling appointed Sun concurrent chief director in the Ministry of Personnel. He was sent out as General Who Pacifies the Distant and governor of Pingzhou. The northern frontier was then in turmoil; he lingered on the road and never took up his post, and was removed from office. Early in Xiaozhuang's reign he was made General Who Assists the State, Regular Attendant of the Fast Cavalry, and eastern-route army supervisor, and sent to suppress the rebel Liu Ju at Puyang—but failed. On his return he was made Attendant of the Fast Cavalry with the additional rank of General of the Vanguard. In the second year of Yong'an he was stripped of rank for having accepted office under Yuan Hao. He was soon restored as General Who Pacifies the Army and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal and Purple Tassel. Under Emperor Chudi he became General of the Guard and Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness. Early in Xiaojing's reign he kept his existing rank, added General of Chariots and Cavalry, and also served as imperial taster and pharmacy supervisor. After some time he was made Minister of Grand Agriculture and fell into repeated mutual accusations with Vice Minister Ma Qingzhe. Sun was keen for profit, and public opinion held him in contempt. He died in the fourth year of Wuding at fifty-six. Posthumously he was granted his former general's rank, the title Minister of Splendid Happiness, and the governorship of Youzhou.
25
子祖微，開府祭酒。 父喪未終，謀反，伏法。
His son Zuo Wei served as libationer of an opening commandery staff. Before his father's mourning period had ended he plotted rebellion and was executed.
26
巒弟儒，瀛州鎮遠府長史、給事中。
Luan's younger brother Ru was chief clerk of Yingzhou's Distance-Pacifying Office and a supervising censor.
27
儒弟偉，尚書郎中。 卒，贈博陵太守。 子昕，在文苑傳。
Ru's younger brother Wei was a gentleman of the Ministry. At his death he was posthumously made governor of Boling. His son Xin is treated in the Literary Garden biography.
28
偉弟季彥。
Wei's younger brother Jiyan.
29
季彥弟晏，字幼平。 美風儀，博涉經史，善談釋老，雅好文詠。 起家太學博士、司徒東閤祭酒。 世宗初，為與廣平王懷遊宴，左遷鄚縣令，未之官。 除給事中，遷司空主簿、本州中正、汝南王文學。 稍遷輔國將軍、司空長史、兼吏部郎中。 以本將軍出為南兗州刺史。 徵為太中大夫、兼丞相高陽王右長史。 尋以本將軍除滄州刺史。 為政清靜，吏民安之。 孝昌中卒，時年五十一。 贈征北將軍、尚書左僕射、瀛州刺史，諡曰文貞。 晏篤於義讓，初為南兗州刺史，例得一子解褐，乃啟其孤弟子子慎，年甫十二，而其子已弱冠矣。 後為滄州，復啟孤兄子昕為府主簿，而其子並未從官。 世人以此多之。
Jiyan's younger brother Yan, courtesy name Youping. Handsome in bearing, widely read in the classics and histories, fluent in Buddhist and Daoist discourse, and devoted to poetry and prose. He began his career as erudite of the Imperial Academy and libationer of the chancellor's Eastern Pavilion. Early in Emperor Xuanwu's reign he was demoted to magistrate of Mo for carousing with Prince Huai of Guangping, but never took up the appointment. He was made supervising censor, then chief clerk of the Ministry of Works, rectifier of his native prefecture, and literary instructor to the Prince of Runan. He rose gradually to General Who Assists the State, chief clerk of the Ministry of Works, and concurrent director in the Ministry of Personnel. With his existing rank he was sent out as governor of Southern Yanzhou. He was recalled as Grand Master of the Palace and concurrent right chief clerk to the Prince of Gaoyang, chancellor of state. Soon afterward he was made governor of Cangzhou, retaining his general's rank. His rule was calm and clean, and officials and people alike lived at ease. He died during the Xiaochang era at fifty-one. Posthumously he was made General Who Campaigns North, Left Vice Director of the Ministry, and governor of Yingzhou, with the posthumous name Wenzhen. Yan was deeply devoted to duty and self-restraint. When he first became governor of Southern Yanzhou, precedent allowed one son to enter office; yet he petitioned for his orphaned brother's son Zishen, then only twelve, though his own son was already twenty. Later, as governor of Cangzhou, he again petitioned for his orphaned elder brother's son Xin as chief clerk of his commandery staff, while his own sons held no office at all. The world praised him widely for this.
30
子測，武定末，太子洗馬。
His son Ce, late in Wuding, was palace groom to the heir apparent.
31
測弟亢，字子高，頗有文學。 釋褐司空行參軍。 遷廣平王開府從事中郎。 兼通直散騎常侍，使於蕭衍，時年二十八。 還，除平東將軍，齊文襄王大將軍府屬，又轉中外府屬。 武定七年，坐事死於晉陽，年三十四。
Ce's younger brother Kang, courtesy name Zigao, was a capable man of letters. On entering office he became a staff adjutant in the Ministry of Works. He was transferred to attendant gentleman on the Prince of Guangping's opening commandery staff. As concurrent Regular Attendant of the Fast Cavalry he was sent as envoy to Xiao Yan at the age of twenty-eight. On his return he was made General Who Pacifies the East and served on the staff of Wenxiang, Prince of Qi, as grand general; he was later transferred to the central and outer offices staff. In the seventh year of Wuding he was executed at Jinyang for an offense, aged thirty-four.
32
巒叔祖祐，字宗祐。 少有學尚，知名於時。 徵除著作郎，領樂浪王傅。 後假員外散騎常侍，使於劉彧。 以將命之勤，除建威將軍、平原太守，賜爵城平男。 政清刑肅，百姓安之。 卒，年七十三。 子產，字神寶。 好學，善屬文。 少時作孤蓬賦，為時所稱。 舉秀才，除著作佐郎。 假員外常侍、鄚縣子，使於蕭賾。 產仍世將命，時人美之。 後遷中書侍郎，俄遷太子中庶子。 卒，年四十六，朝廷嗟惜焉。 贈建威將軍、平州刺史、樂城子，諡曰定。
Luan's granduncle You, courtesy name Zongyou. From youth he pursued learning and won renown in his day. Summoned to office, he was made gentleman for compilation and concurrently tutor to the Prince of Lelang. He was later made Acting Regular Attendant of the Fast Cavalry and sent as envoy to Liu Yu. For faithful service on his mission he was made General Who Establishes Might and governor of Pingyuan, and enfeoffed as Baron of Chengping. His rule was honest and his punishments firm, and the people lived in peace. He died at the age of seventy-three. His son Chan, courtesy name Shenbao. He was devoted to learning and skilled at writing. In his youth he wrote the "Rhapsody on the Lone Tumbleweed," which won contemporary acclaim. Recommended as Cultivated Talent, he was appointed Assistant Editor of the Palace Library. Granted acting rank as Supernumerary Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and made Viscount of Mo County, he was sent on mission to Xiao Ze of Southern Qi. For generations the family had borne imperial commissions, and contemporaries admired Chan for continuing the tradition. He was later promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat and soon afterward to Chief Attendant of the Heir Apparent. He died at forty-six, to the court's deep regret. He was posthumously honored as General Who Establishes Might, Governor of Pingzhou, and Viscount of Lecheng, with the posthumous title Ding ("Settled").
33
祐從子虬，字神虎。 少為三禮鄭氏學，明經有文思。 舉秀才上第，為中書議郎、尚書殿中郎。 高祖因公事與語，問朝覲宴饗之禮，虬以經對，大合上旨。 轉司徒屬、國子博士。 高祖崩，尚書令王肅多用新儀，虬往往折以五經正禮。 轉尚書右丞，徙左丞，多所糾正，臺閣肅然。 時雁門人有害母者，八座奏轘之而潴其室，宥其二子。 虬駁奏云：「君親無將，將而必誅。 今謀逆者戮及期親，害親者今不及子，既逆甚梟鏡，禽獸之不若，而使禋祀不絕，遺育永傳，非所以勸忠孝之道，存三綱之義。 若聖教含容，不加孥戮，使父子罪不相及，惡止於其身，不則宜投之四裔，敕所在不聽配匹。 盤庚言『無令易種於新邑』，漢法五月食梟羹，皆欲絕其類也。 」奏入，世宗從之。 尋除司徒右長史，遷龍驤將軍、光祿少卿。 虬母在鄉遇患，請假歸。 值秋水暴長，河梁破絕，虬得一小船而渡，漏而不沒，時人異之。 母喪，哀毀過禮，為時所稱。 年四十九，卒。 贈征虜將軍、幽州刺史，諡曰威。 虬善與人交，清河崔亮、頓丘李平並與親善。 所作碑頌雜筆三十餘篇。 有二子。
You's nephew Qiu, courtesy name Shenhu. In youth he studied the Three Rites in Zheng Xuan's tradition; he mastered the classics and possessed literary gifts. Graduating first in the Cultivated Talent examination, he was appointed Secretariat Discussion Officer and Palace Attendant in the Ministry of State Affairs. On official business Emperor Xiaowen spoke with him and asked about the rites of imperial audiences and banquets. Qiu answered from the classics in a manner that pleased the emperor greatly. He was transferred to the staff of the Minister of Education and appointed Erudite of the Imperial University. After Emperor Xiaowen's death, Minister of State Wang Su often introduced new ritual forms, but Qiu repeatedly countered with the orthodox rites of the Five Classics. Promoted from Right to Left Vice Director of the Ministry, he corrected many abuses and brought order to the central government. When a man of Yanmen murdered his mother, the Eight Excellencies recommended that he be torn apart by chariot and his house inundated, while sparing his two sons. Qiu submitted a rebuttal: "Between ruler and parent there can be no insubordination—and once insubordination appears, death is certain. Today rebels are punished together with their closest kin, yet a man who kills his parent is not punished through his sons. Though such a crime surpasses even the owl and the mirror—worse than any beast—we would still let his sacrifices continue and his line endure forever. That is no way to encourage loyalty and filial piety or uphold the Three Bonds. If the sage teaching is merciful and does not punish offspring, then let father and son not answer for one another's crimes, and let guilt end with the guilty. Otherwise the offenders should be banished to the four borderlands, with orders that no one in those regions may marry them. Pan Geng said, 'Do not let them change their seed in the new city,' and Han law required eating owl soup in the fifth month—both measures meant to cut off a wicked line. " When the memorial was submitted, Emperor Xuanwu agreed. He was soon appointed Right Chief of Staff to the Minister of Education, then promoted to Dragon-Cavalry General and Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments. When Qiu's mother fell ill at home in the countryside, he asked for leave to return. Autumn floods had burst the river banks and destroyed the bridge. Qiu found a small boat and crossed; though it leaked, it did not sink, and people regarded this as remarkable. When his mother died, his grief exceeded what the rites prescribed, and contemporaries praised his filial devotion. He died at the age of forty-nine. He was posthumously honored as General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Governor of Youzhou, with the posthumous title Wei ("Authoritative"). Qiu was gifted at friendship and was close to Cui Liang of Qinghe and Li Ping of Dunqiu. He left more than thirty stele inscriptions, eulogies, and assorted writings. He had two sons.
34
長子臧，在文苑傳。
His eldest son Zang is treated in the Treatise on Literature.
35
臧弟子才，武定末，太常卿。
Zang's nephew Cai served as Minister of Imperial Sacrifices at the end of the Wuding era.
36
虬從子策，亦有才學。 卒於齊王儀同開府主簿。
Qiu's nephew Ce was also a man of talent and learning. He died while serving as Chief Clerk of the Prince of Qi's General-in-Chief headquarters.
37
李平，字曇定，頓丘人也，彭城王嶷之長子。 少有大度。 及長，涉獵羣書，好禮、易，頗有文才。 太和初，拜通直散騎侍郎，高祖禮之甚重。 頻經大憂，居喪以孝稱。 後以例降，襲爵彭城公。 拜太子中舍人，遷散騎侍郎，舍人如故，遷太子中庶子。 平因侍從容請自效一郡，高祖曰：「卿復欲以吏事自試也。 」拜長樂太守，政務清靜，吏民懷之。 車駕南伐，以平兼冀州儀同開府長史，甚著聲稱，仍除正長史，太守如故。 未幾，遂行河南尹，豪右權貴憚之。 世宗即位，除黃門郎，遷司徒左長史，行尹如故。 尋以稱職正尹，長史如故。
Li Ping, courtesy name Tanding, came from Dunqiu. He was the eldest son of Prince Pengcheng Yi. Even as a youth he was broad-minded and generous. As he matured he read widely, loved the Rites and the Book of Changes, and showed considerable literary talent. At the opening of the Taihe era he was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary of Direct Communication, and Emperor Xiaowen held him in high regard. Having endured repeated bereavements, he was renowned for filial devotion in mourning. Later, following the usual reduction in rank, he inherited the title Duke of Pengcheng. He was appointed Attendant of the Heir Apparent, then promoted to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary while retaining his attendant post, and later to Chief Attendant of the Heir Apparent. While attending the emperor, Li Ping calmly asked to prove himself in a single commandery. Emperor Xiaowen said, "So you wish to test yourself in administrative affairs again. " He was appointed Administrator of Changle. His administration was honest and tranquil, and officials and commoners alike held him in affection. During the southern campaign, Li Ping was additionally appointed Chief of Staff to the Jizhou General-in-Chief headquarters, where he won great renown. He was soon made regular chief of staff while continuing as Administrator. Before long he was appointed acting Director of Henan, where powerful families and grasping officials feared him. When Emperor Xuanwu ascended the throne, Li Ping was appointed Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and promoted to Left Chief of Staff to the Minister of Education while continuing as acting Director of Henan. Soon, recognized for his competence, he was made regular Director of Henan while continuing as Chief of Staff.
38
車駕將幸鄴，平上表諫曰：「伏見己丑詔書，雲軒鑾輅，行幸有期，鳳服龍驂，剋駕近日。 將欲講武淇陽，大習鄴魏，馳驌騻於綠竹之區，騁驎驥於漳滏之壤。 斯誠幽顯同忻，人靈共悅。 臣之愚管，竊有惑焉。 何者？ 嵩京創構，洛邑俶營，雖年跨十稔，根基未就。 代民至洛，始欲向盡，資產罄於遷移，牛畜斃於輦運，陵太行之險，越長津之難，辛勤備經，得達京闕，富者猶損太半，貧者可以意知。 兼歷歲從戎，不遑啟處，自景明已來，差得休息。 事農者未積二年之儲，築室者裁有數間之屋，莫不肆力伊瀍，人急其務。 實宜安靜新人，勸其稼穡，令國有九年之糧，家有水旱之備。 若乘之以羈紲，則所廢多矣。 一夫從役，舉家失業。 今復秋稼盈田，禾菽遍野，鑾駕所幸，騰踐必殷。 未若端拱中天，坐招四海，耀武崧原，禮射伊洛，士馬無跋涉之勞，兆民有康哉之詠，可不美歟？ 」不從。 詔以本官行相州事。 世宗至鄴，親幸平第，見其諸子。 尋正刺史，加征虜將軍。
When the emperor was about to visit Ye, Li Ping submitted a memorial of remonstrance: "I have read the edict of the jichou day: the cloud-canopied carriage and imperial palanquin are to set out on a fixed date; phoenix-robed attendants and dragon-harnessed steeds will depart within days. Your Majesty intends to review troops at Qiyang and hold great exercises in Ye and Wei—to gallop fine horses through the groves of green bamboo and race thoroughbreds across the banks of the Zhang and Fu. This would indeed bring joy to spirits and men alike. Yet in my limited understanding I cannot help but harbor doubts. Why? The new capital at Songshan and the city of Luoyang have both been under construction for more than ten years, yet their foundations are still unfinished. The people of Dai who came to Luoyang had scarcely arrived before their resources were exhausted. Their goods were spent in the move, their oxen and livestock died on the road, and after braving the peril of Taihang and the long river crossings they reached the capital only after every hardship. Even the wealthy lost more than half their property; the poor fared far worse. For years they have served in the army without respite. Only since the Jingming era have they had any real rest. Farmers have not yet stored two years' grain; those building houses have scarcely a few rooms to their name. All are laboring along the Yi and Chan rivers, each pressed by urgent tasks. Surely it is time to let these newcomers settle, encourage their farming, and build up nine years' grain for the state and reserves against flood and drought for every household. If they are yoked to corvée and service again, much will be lost. When one man is called to service, the whole household loses its livelihood. Autumn crops now fill the fields and grain covers the countryside. Wherever the imperial procession passes, the trampling will be severe. Would it not be better to sit in dignity at the center of the realm and summon the four seas, display martial glory on the Song plain, and perform the archery rites at Yi and Luo—so that soldiers and horses need not weary themselves with long marches and the people may sing of peace? What could be more fitting? " The emperor did not heed him. An edict appointed him to administer Xiangzhou affairs in his current rank. When Emperor Xuanwu reached Ye, he personally visited Li Ping's home and met his sons. He was soon made regular governor and additionally granted the title General Who Subdues the Barbarians.
39
平勸課農桑，修飾太學，簡試通儒以充博士，選五郡聰敏者以教之，圖孔子及七十二子於堂，親為立讚。 前來臺使頗好侵取，平乃畫「履虎尾」、「踐薄冰」於客館，注頌其下，以示誡焉。 加平東將軍，徵拜長兼度支尚書，尋正尚書，領御史中尉。
Li Ping promoted agriculture and sericulture, restored the Imperial University, selected accomplished Confucian scholars as erudites, recruited clever students from five commanderies to study under them, and had Confucius and the seventy-two disciples painted in the hall, composing encomia for each himself. Envoys from the capital were prone to extortion, so Li Ping had "Treading a Tiger's Tail" and "Walking on Thin Ice" painted in the guest lodge with explanatory verses beneath—a pointed warning. He was additionally made General Who Pacifies the East, then summoned to serve concurrently and as regular Director of the Ministry of Revenue; soon made regular director while also holding the post of Inspector-in-Chief.
40
冀州刺史、京兆王愉反於信都，以平為使持節、都督北討諸軍事、鎮北將軍，行冀州事以討之。 世宗臨式乾殿，勞遣平曰：「愉，朕之元弟，居不疑之地，豺狼之心，不意而發，欲上傾社稷，下殘萬姓。 大義滅親，夫豈獲止。 周公行之於古，朕亦當行之於今。 委卿以專征之任，必令應期摧殄，務盡經略之規，勿虧推轂之寄也。 何圖今日言及斯事。 」因歔欷流涕。 平對曰：「臣愉天迷其心，構此梟悖。 陛下不以臣不武，委以總督之任，今大宥既敷，便應有征無戰。 脫守迷不悟者，當仰憑天威，抑厲將士，譬猶太陽之消微露，巨海之蕩熒燭，天時人事，滅在昭然。 如其稽顙軍門，則送之大理，若不悛待戮，則鳴鼓釁鍾，非陛下之事。」
When Jizhou Governor and Prince of Jingzhao Yu rebelled at Xindu, Li Ping was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commander of Northern Expeditionary Forces, and General Who Pacifies the North, with authority over Jizhou affairs to suppress the rebellion. At the Shiqian Hall, Emperor Xuanwu bid Li Ping farewell with these words: "Yu is my own brother, placed in a position beyond suspicion. Yet a wolf's heart has burst forth unlooked-for: he would overturn the altars of state above and slaughter the people below. When great righteousness demands the destruction of kin, who may hold back? The Duke of Zhou did this in antiquity; I must do the same today. I entrust you with sole command. You must destroy him at the appointed time, carry out every measure of strategy, and not betray the trust I place in you as my chosen commander. Who would have thought I would ever have to speak of such a thing. " With that he sighed and wept. Li Ping replied, "Yu has lost his mind to heaven and raised this wicked rebellion. Your Majesty, not deeming me unfit for war, has entrusted me with overall command. Now that the great pardon has been proclaimed, the campaign should require no fighting. If any hold out in stubborn delusion, I shall rely on Heaven's majesty and steel the troops—as the sun dispels morning dew, as the great sea washes away a flickering candle. Heaven and human affairs alike make their destruction plain. If they prostrate themselves at the army gate, I shall send them to the Court of Justice. If they refuse to repent and await execution, then drums will sound and bells be struck—that will be no affair of Your Majesty's."
41
平進次經縣，諸軍大集。 夜有蠻兵數千斫平前壘，矢及平帳，平堅臥不動，俄而乃定。 遂至冀州城南十六里。 賊攻圍濟州軍，拔柵填塹，未滿者數尺。 諸將合戰，無利而還，憚於更進。 平親入行間，勸以重賞，士卒乃前，大破逆眾。 愉時墜馬，乃有一人下馬授愉，止而鬬死。 乘勝逐北，至於城門，斬首數萬級，遂圍城燒門。 愉與百餘騎突門出走，遣統軍叔孫頭追之，去信都十里擒愉。 冀州平，世宗遣兼給事黃門侍郎、祕書丞元梵宣旨慰勞。 徵還京師，以本官領相州大中正。
Li Ping advanced and encamped at Jing County, where the armies assembled in force. By night several thousand tribal soldiers attacked Li Ping's forward rampart; arrows struck his tent, yet he lay still and did not stir until the disturbance subsided. He then reached a point sixteen li south of Jizhou city. The rebels attacked and besieged the Jizhou army, tearing up palisades and filling the moat until only a few chi remained unfilled. The generals joined battle but gained no advantage and withdrew, afraid to press forward again. Li Ping personally entered the ranks and promised heavy rewards. The soldiers then pressed forward and routed the rebel force. Yu fell from his horse; a man dismounted, gave Yu his own mount, and fought to the death where he stood. Pursuing the victory northward to the city gate, they took tens of thousands of heads, then besieged the city and set fire to the gate. Yu broke out of the gate with a little over a hundred horsemen. Li Ping sent Commander Shusun Tou in pursuit and captured Yu ten li from Xindu. When Jizhou was pacified, Emperor Xuanwu dispatched Concurrent Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gate and Secretary Director Yuan Fan to convey the imperial message and offer congratulations. He was recalled to the capital and, retaining his present office, was also made Chief Rectifier of Xiangzhou.
42
平先為尚書令高肇、侍御史王顯所恨，後顯代平為中尉，平加散騎常侍，顯劾平在冀州隱截官口，肇又扶成其狀，奏除平名。 延昌初，詔復官爵，除其定冀之勳。 前來良賤之訟，多有積年不決，平奏不問真偽，一以景明年前為限，於是諍訟止息。 武川鎮民飢，鎮將任款請貸未許，擅開倉賑恤，有司繩以費散之條，免其官爵。 平奏款意在濟人，心無不善，世宗原之。 遷中書令，尚書如故。 肅宗初，轉吏部尚書，加撫軍將軍。 平高明強濟，所在有聲，但以性急為累。 尚書令、任城王澄奏理平定冀之勳，請酬以山河之賞。 靈太后乃封武邑郡開國公，食邑一千五百戶，縑二千五百匹。
Li Ping had long been hated by Minister of State Gao Zhao and Attendant Censor Wang Xian. When Xian replaced Ping as Inspector-in-Chief, Ping was additionally made Regular Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary. Xian then impeached him for concealing and intercepting registered corvée laborers in Jizhou; Gao helped establish the case, and a memorial was submitted stripping Li Ping of his office and rank. At the beginning of the Yan chang era, an edict restored his office and title but stripped him of his merit for pacifying Jizhou. Lawsuits over free and servile status had often dragged on unresolved for years. Li Ping memorialized that such cases, without inquiry into truth or falsehood, be limited to those arising before the Jingming era. Contentious litigation then ceased. When the people of Wuchuan Garrison faced famine, Garrison Commander Ren Kuan requested grain on loan but was refused; he opened the granary on his own authority to relieve them. The responsible offices charged him under the statute on wasteful dispersal of stores and stripped him of office and rank. Li Ping memorialized that Ren Kuan's intent had been to save the people and that his heart held no evil. Emperor Xuanwu pardoned him. He was transferred to Director of the Secretariat while retaining his ministry post. At the beginning of Emperor Xiaoming's reign, he was transferred to Minister of the Ministry of Personnel and additionally made General Who Pacifies the Army. Li Ping was gifted, forceful, and capable; he earned a reputation wherever he served, though his impetuous temperament was his one flaw. Director of the Secretariat Yuan Cheng, Prince of Rencheng, submitted a memorial settling the record of Li Ping's pacification of Ji and asking that he be rewarded with a territorial enfeoffment. Empress Dowager Ling then created him Duke of Wuyi commandery with state-founding rank, granting a fief of fifteen hundred households and twenty-five hundred bolts of silk.
43
先是，蕭衍遣其左游擊將軍趙祖悅偷據西硤石，眾至數萬，以逼壽春。 鎮南崔亮攻之，未克，又與李崇乖貳。 詔平以本官使持節、鎮軍大將軍、兼尚書右僕射為行臺，節度諸軍，東西州將一以禀之，如有乖異，以軍法從事。 詔平長子奬以通直郎從，賜平縑帛百段、紫納金裝衫甲一領，賜奬縑布六十段、絳衲襖一領。 父子重列，拜受家庭，觀者榮之。 於是率步騎二千以赴壽春。 平巡視硤石內外，知其盈虛之所。 嚴勒崇、亮，令水陸兼備，剋期齊舉。 崇、亮憚之，無敢乖互。 頻日交戰，屢破賊軍。 安南將軍崔延伯立橋於下蔡，以拒賊之援軍。 賊將王神念、昌義之等不得進救，祖悅守死窮城。 平乃部分攻之。 令崔亮督陸卒攻其城西，李崇勒水軍擊其東面，然後鼓噪，南北俱上。 賊眾周章，東西赴戰。 屠賊外城，賊之將士相率歸附。 袓悅率其餘眾固保南城，通夜攻守，至明乃降。 斬袓悅，送首於洛，俘獲甚眾。 以功遷尚書右僕射，加散騎常侍，將軍如故。
Earlier, Xiao Yan had sent his Left Mobile General Zhao Zu Yue to seize West Xiashi by surprise; his army numbered in the tens of thousands and threatened Shouchun. Cui Liang, Pacifier of the South, besieged him without success, and he also fell out with Li Chong. An edict appointed Li Ping, retaining his existing rank, as Commissioner Bearing Credentials, General Who Guards the Army, and concurrent Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, with authority as mobile headquarters over all armies. Generals of the eastern and western provinces were to take orders from him alone, and any who defied him were to be punished under military law. An edict appointed Li Ping's eldest son Jiang Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary to accompany him. Li Ping received one hundred bolts of silk and brocade and a suit of purple padded armor with gold fittings; Jiang received sixty bolts of silk and hemp and a padded jacket of crimson cloth. Father and son stood side by side to bow and receive the imperial gifts at home, to the envy of all who watched. He then led two thousand foot and horse to Shouchun. Li Ping surveyed Xiashi inside and out and learned where its strengths and weaknesses lay. He pressed Li Chong and Cui Liang hard, ordering land and water forces alike made ready to attack together on the fixed day. Li Chong and Cui Liang feared him and no longer dared to work at cross purposes. Battle followed battle for days on end, and the rebel army was broken again and again. Cui Yanbo, General Who Pacifies the South, built a bridge at Xia Cai to block the rebels' relief force. The rebel generals Wang Shennian, Chang Yizhi, and others could not break through to relieve the city; Zu Yue held the hopeless fortress to the last. Li Ping then divided his forces and pressed the assault. He ordered Cui Liang to lead the infantry against the west wall and Li Chong to drive the fleet against the east; then, at the war cry, both wings surged forward together. The rebel host fell into confusion and rushed back and forth between east and west. They stormed the outer city, and rebel officers and soldiers surrendered in waves. Zu Yue gathered his remaining men in the south city and fought through the night; at dawn he surrendered. Zu Yue was beheaded and his head sent to Luoyang; the prisoners taken were very many. For this achievement he was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, while retaining his general's commission.
44
平還京師，靈太后見於宣光殿，賜以金裝刀杖一口。 時南徐州表云，蕭衍堰淮水為患，詔公卿議之，平以為不假兵力，終自毀壞。 及淮堰破，靈太后大悅，引群臣入宴，敕平前鳴簫管，肅宗手賜縑布百段。 熙平元年冬卒，遺令薄葬。 詔給東園祕器、朝服一具、衣一襲、帛七百匹。 靈太后為舉哀於東堂。 贈侍中、驃騎大將軍、儀同三司、冀州刺史，諡文烈公。 平自在度支，至於端副，夙夜在公，孜孜匪懈，凡處機密十有餘年，有獻替之稱。 所製詩賦箴諫詠頌，[13]別有集錄。
When Li Ping returned to the capital, Empress Dowager Ling received him in the Hall of Illuminated Glory and granted him a sword and staff with gold fittings. Southern Xuzhou then reported that Xiao Yan's dam on the Huai was causing damage. The court ordered the high officials to debate the matter, and Li Ping argued that it needed no troops and would collapse of its own accord. When the Huai dam gave way, Empress Dowager Ling was delighted. She brought the ministers in to feast, had Li Ping step forward to play pipes and flutes, and Emperor Xiaozong personally granted him one hundred bolts of silk and hemp. He died in the winter of Xiping 1, leaving orders for a simple burial. An edict granted him the eastern garden secret coffin, one set of court robes, one suit of clothing, and seven hundred bolts of silk. Empress Dowager Ling held mourning rites for him in the Eastern Hall. He was posthumously honored as Palace Attendant, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, with an office equal to the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Ji province, with the posthumous epithet Duke Wenlie. From his years as Director of Revenue to his tenure at the apex of government, Li Ping rose early and worked late, tireless in office; for more than ten years he handled state secrets and was praised for counsel that improved policy. The poems, rhapsodies, admonitions, remonstrances, songs, and eulogies he composed [13] were gathered in a separate collection.
45
平長子奬，字遵穆，襲。 容貌魁偉，有當世才度。 自太尉參軍事，稍遷通直郎、中書侍郎、直閤將軍、吏部郎中、征虜將軍，遷安東將軍、光祿大夫，仍吏部郎中。 又以本官兼尚書，出為撫軍將軍、相州刺史。 初，元叉擅朝，奬為其親待，頻居顯要。 靈太后反政，削除官爵。 孝莊初，為散騎常侍、鎮東將軍、河南尹。 奬前後所歷，皆以明濟著稱。 元顥入洛，顥以奬兼尚書右僕射，慰勞徐州羽林及城人，不承顥旨，害奬，傳首洛陽。
Li Ping's eldest son Jiang, courtesy name Zunmu, succeeded to his father's rank. He was tall and imposing in bearing, with the talent and stature to match his times. Beginning as an aide to the Grand Commandant, he rose step by step through Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, Vice Director of the Secretariat, General of the Direct Gate, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and General Who Punishes the Barbarians, then to General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and again Director of the Ministry of Personnel. He was then made Concurrent Director of the Secretariat in his existing rank and sent out as General Who Pacifies the Army and Governor of Xiang province. When Yuan Cha first dominated the court, Jiang was treated as a close favorite and repeatedly held high office. When Empress Dowager Ling resumed power, his offices and titles were stripped away. At the start of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign he was appointed Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Pacifies the East, and Governor of Henan. In every post he had held, Jiang was known for clear and effective governance. When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, he made Jiang Concurrent Right Vice Director of the Secretariat to reassure the Xuzhou guard and the city's people; they refused Hao's orders, killed Jiang, and sent his head to Luoyang.
46
出帝時，奬故吏通直散騎常侍宋遊道上書理奬曰：「臣聞賞善罰惡，謂之二機，有道存焉，所貴不濫。 是以子胥無罪，吳人痛之； 郤宛不幸，國言未息。 故河南尹李奬，門居戚里，世擅名家，有此良才，是兼周用。 自少及長，忠孝為心，入朝出牧，清明流譽。 襟懷放暢，風神爽發，實廊廟之瑚璉，社稷之楨幹。 往歲，北海竊據，負扆當朝，王公卿士，俛眉從事。 而奬闔門百口，同居京洛，既被覊縶，自拔無由。 託使東南，情存避難，當時物論謂其得所。 然北海未敗之日，徐州刺史元孚為其純臣，莫之敢距，表啟相望，遲速唯命。 及皇輿返正，神器斯復，輕薄之徒，共生僥倖，詭言要賞，曲道求通，濫及善人，稱為己力。 若以奬受命賊朝，語跡成罪，便與天下共當此責。 于時朝旨唯命免官，亦既經恩，方加酷濫。 伊昔具臣，比肩賊所，身臨河上，日尋干戈，時逢寬政，任遇不改。 一介使人，獨嬰斯戮，凡在有心，孰不嗟悼！ 前朝所以論功者，見其邊人且相慰悅，其猶郭默生亂，劉胤懸首，事乃權宜，蓋非實錄。 昔鄧艾下世，段灼理其冤； 馬援物故，朱勃申其屈。 臣雖小人，趣事君子，有懷舊恩，義兼人故，見其若此，久欲陳辭。 含言未吐，遂至今日，幽泉已閉，壟樹成行，內手捫心，顧懷愧慨。 幸逢興聖，理運唯新，雖曰纂戎，事同創革。 頻有大恩，被於率土，亡官失爵者悉蒙追復。 而奬雜木猶存，牛車未改。 士感知己，懷此無忘，輕率瞽言，干犯輦轂。 伏願天鑒，賜垂矜覽，加其贈秩，慰此幽魂。 」詔贈衞將軍、冀州刺史。
During the reign of the Deposed Emperor, Jiang's former subordinate Song Youdao, Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Direct Gate, submitted a memorial in his defense, saying: "Your subject has heard that rewarding good and punishing evil are the two levers of rule; the Way rests in them, and what matters is that they never be misapplied. When Wu Zixu was innocent, the people of Wu grieved for him; when Xi Wan met with misfortune, the kingdom's lament never ceased. The former Governor of Henan, Li Jiang, belonged to the imperial kin; his family had long been a house of renown, and with such talent he was fit for every task. From youth to age loyalty and filial piety filled his heart; whether at court or governing a province, he won fame for clarity. Open in spirit and bright in bearing, he was truly a ritual vessel of the court and a pillar of the state. In years past, when Beihai seized power and held the throne, princes, dukes, ministers, and officials all bowed and obeyed. Yet Jiang's household of a hundred mouths lived together in the capital; once bound and held captive, he had no way to break free. Sent on a mission to the southeast, he sought refuge from disaster; public opinion at the time held that he had chosen wisely. Yet before Beihai's defeat, Xuzhou Governor Yuan Fu was his loyal servant and none dared resist him; memorial after memorial went out, and every move awaited his command. When the throne was restored and the sacred vessel recovered, frivolous men seized on vain hopes; with twisted words they claimed reward, by crooked paths they sought favor, and they dragged good men into guilt and called it their own merit. If accepting office under the rebel court makes Jiang guilty by word and deed, then the whole realm must bear that guilt together. At the time the court's intent was only to dismiss him from office; having already shown mercy, they then added cruel excess. In former times worthy ministers stood side by side in the rebel camp, themselves on the riverbank day after day at war; when leniency prevailed, their appointments were unchanged. One lone envoy alone suffered this execution; all who have a heart—who could fail to mourn him! The previous court counted it merit only because the border people seemed somewhat reassured; it was like when Guo Mo raised rebellion and Liu Yin's head was displayed—the affair was expedient and hardly a true record. In the past, when Deng Ai died, Duan Zhuo cleared his wrong; when Ma Yuan passed away, Zhu Bo pleaded his grievance. Your subject, though a humble man, has always wished to serve the worthy; cherishing old kindness and bound by friendship, seeing Jiang treated thus, he has long wished to speak out. Words held back have reached this day; the grave is closed and tomb trees stand in rows; pressing hand to heart, he looks back with shame and grief. Fortunately we meet a sage ascending the throne and an age wholly renewed; though called succession, the work is like a new founding. Great grace has repeatedly spread over the realm; all who lost office and rank have been restored. Yet Jiang, like a withered stump, still stands unrewarded, and the humble cart of his rank is unchanged. A gentleman who knows kindness cannot forget this; with rash and reckless words he offends the imperial presence. Prostrate, he prays that Heaven's mirror may grant pity and review, adding to Jiang's posthumous rank to comfort his shade. " An edict posthumously honored him as General of the Guard and Governor of Ji province.
47
子構，襲。 武定末，太子中舍人。 齊受禪，爵例降。
His son Gou succeeded to the title. At the end of the Wuding era he served as Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Heir Apparent. When Qi accepted the abdication, his rank was reduced according to precedent.
48
構弟訓，太尉默曹參軍。
Gou's younger brother Xun was a staff officer in the Grand Commandant's Secretariat.
49
奬弟諧，字虔和。 風流閑潤，博學有文辯，當時才俊，咸相欽賞。 受父前爵彭城侯。 自太尉參軍，歷尚書郎、徐州北海王顥撫軍府司馬，入為長兼中書侍郎。 崔光引為兼著作郎，諧在史職，無所歷意。 加輔國將軍、相州大中正、光祿大夫，除金紫光祿大夫，加衞將軍。 元顥入洛，以為給事黃門侍郎。 顥敗，除名，乃為述身賦曰：
Jiang's younger brother Xie, courtesy name Qianhe. Graceful, refined, and easy in manner, broadly learned and eloquent in writing, he was admired by every talented man of the age. He inherited his father's former title, Marquis of Pengcheng. Starting as an aide to the Grand Commandant, he served as Director of the Secretariat, then as Sima on the Pacification Army staff of Yuan Hao, Prince of Beihai, in Xuzhou, and entered court as Senior Concurrent Vice Director of the Secretariat. Cui Guang brought him in as Concurrent Compiler in the History Office, but Xie had no heart for historiography. He was promoted to General Who Supports the State, Chief Rectifier of Xiang province, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, then appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Purple Seal and General of the Guard. When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gate. When Hao was defeated, his name was struck from the rolls, and he composed a Rhapsody on Describing My Life, saying:
50
夫休咎相躡，禍福相生。 龜筮迷其兆，聖達蔽其萌。 覽成敗於前迹，料趣捨於人情。 咸爭途以走利，罕外己以逃名。 連從車以載禍，多廐馬以取刑。 豈知夫一介獨往，乃千乘所不能傾。 伊薄躬之悔吝，無性命之淑靈。 藉休庸於祖武，仰餘烈於家聲。 徒從師以下學，乏遊道於上京。 洎方年之四五，實始筮之弱齡。 爰釋巾而從吏，謬邀寵於時明。
Fortune and misfortune tread on each other's heels; disaster and blessing beget one another. Tortoise shells and milfoil stalks fail their omens; even sages cannot see the first sprout. Men read success and failure in the tracks of the past and weigh advance and retreat by human feeling. All race the road to profit; few turn outward from self to flee fame. They link follow-carts to carry disaster and keep many stable horses to invite punishment. How could they know that one man going alone cannot be overturned even by a thousand chariots? Alas for my slight person and its regrets—I have no inborn grace of life. I lean on my ancestors' martial merit and look up to the lingering glory of our family name. In vain I followed teachers in humble study; I never found the way to wander and learn in the capital. When my years reached four or five, it was truly the tender age of first divination. Then I put aside the scholar's towel and followed the clerks, wrongly seeking favor in a bright age.
51
彼□□之赫赫，乃陋周而小漢。 帝文篤其成功，我武治其未亂。 掩四奧而同軌，穆三辰而貞觀。 威北暢而武戢，鼎南遷而文煥。 異人相趨於絳闕，鴻生接武於儒館。 總羣雅而同歸，果方員而殊貫。 伊濫吹之所從，初竊服於宰旅。 奉盛王之高義，遊兔園而容與。 綴鴻鷺之末行，連英髦之茂序。
That □□'s splendor made Zhou seem small and Han petty. Imperial culture secured its achievement; our martial virtue ordered what was not yet in disorder. It covered the four quarters and made one track; it harmonized sun, moon, and stars and kept the realm in right order. Its might flowed north and arms were stilled; the cauldron moved south and culture blazed. Strange men hastened to the crimson gate; great scholars walked in succession at the halls of learning. Gathering all elegance to one end, square and round in form yet threaded on different strings. From the indiscriminate piping I followed, at first I stole a place among the host of clerks. Honoring the Prince of Sheng's high righteousness, I wandered at ease in the Rabbit Garden. I joined the last rank of wild swans and geese and linked the flourishing order of outstanding men.

及伯舅之西伐，赫靈旗之東舉。 復奉役於前轅，仍執覊於後距。 迫玄冬之暮歲，歷關山之遐阻。 風激沙而破石，雪浮河而漫野。 樂在志其無端，悲涉物而多緒。 俄宮車之晏駕，改乘轅而歸予。
When the emperor's maternal uncle marched west and the blazing imperial banner was raised in the east. Again I served at the front axle and still was held in bonds at the rear guard. In the deep of dark winter's last days, I crossed the far barriers of the mountain passes. Wind lashed the sand and shattered stone; snow drifted on the rivers and flooded the plain. Joy rose in the heart without reason; grief touched every thing and bred a tangle of feeling. Then the imperial carriage halted in death, and I changed my axle-shaft and turned homeward.

屬推恩之在今，自傍枝而禔福。 既獻□以命宗，叨微躬於侯服。 禮空文於覜饗，賦無征於湯沐。 思守位而匪懈，每屏居而自肅。 忽忝命於建禮，遊丹綺之重複。 信茲選之為難，乃上應於列宿。 陽源猶且自免，何稱仲治與太叔。 余生□之蕭散，本寓名而為仕。 好不存於吏法，才實疏於政理。 竟火燭之不事，徒博弈其賢已。 竊自託於諸生，頗馳騁於文史。 通人假其餘論，士林察於□理。 乃妄涉於風流，遂飾輩於士子。 且以自託，□□□□。
In the season of extended grace, I—a branch of a collateral line—received its blessings. Having presented □ to ennoble the ancestral house, I undeservedly received a minor place among the enfeoffed lords. Court audiences were empty ceremony at inspection feasts; feudal dues brought no revenue even for bath grants. I resolved to hold my post without slackening, and each time I withdrew to seclusion and kept myself in check. Suddenly I was undeservedly appointed at the Jianli Gate and wandered the layered halls of cinnabar and brocade. Truly this appointment was a hard choice—it even had to answer to the stars above. Even Yang Yuan excused himself from office—how could one be called Zhongzhi or Taishu? My remaining life is □ and free of care; I had only lent my name to office in the first place. My tastes had no place in clerkly law, and my talent was truly thin for governing affairs. In the end I did not burn the midnight oil at urgent business; I merely played chess to prove my worth. Secretly I cast my lot with the scholars and ranged freely through literature and history. Men of insight borrowed my spare arguments; the forest of scholars judged me by □ principle. Then I rashly entered the world of elegant letters and at last passed myself off among gentlemen. And so I entrusted myself □□□□.
