雖邇傒塵滓，而賞許雲霞。 栖閑虛以築館，背城闕而為家。 帶二學之高宇，遠三市之狹邪。 事雖儉而未陋，製有度而不奢。 山隱勢於複石，水回流於激沙。 樹先春而動色，草迎歲而發花。 座有清談之客，門交好事之車。 或林嬉於月夜，或水宴於景斜。 肆雕章之腴旨，咀文藝之英華。 羞綠芰與丹藕，薦朱李及甘瓜。 雖慚洛水之名致，有類金谷之諠譁。 聊自足於所好，豈留連於或號。 思炯戒而自反，勗身名於所蹈。 奉哲后之淵猷，讚崇麾於華奧。 豈千乘之乏使，感一眄之相勞。 竟不留於三月，因病滿而休告。
Though I stood near the dust and mire, men praised me as high as cloud and rosy light. I dwelt in leisure and built a hall apart, turning my back on the city gate to make a home. It bordered the high halls of the two academies and stood far from the narrow lanes of the three markets. The place was plain yet not crude; its design had measure and was never extravagant. Mountains hid their slopes in layered stone; water turned back in eddies over rushing sand. Trees stirred with color before spring; grass met the new year and sent forth flowers. Within sat guests of pure discourse; at the gate came carriages of men who loved fine things. Some frolicked in the groves by moonlight; some feasted on the water as the light slanted. They unfolded the rich flavor of carved prose and savored the flower of literary art. They set out green water-chestnuts and red lotus roots and offered red plums and sweet melons. Though I fell short of the fame of the Luo waters, it still resembled the clamor of the Golden Valley. For a time it was enough for what I loved—how could I linger for some empty title? I took bright warning and turned back on myself, urging body and name along the path I trod. Serving the sage ruler's deep design, I praised the lofty banner in the splendid inner court. Was it that a thousand chariots lacked envoys? I was moved by a single glance and personal labor. In the end I did not remain three months; when my sick leave was exhausted I asked to withdraw.

彼東觀之清華，乃任隆於載筆。 蔡一去而貽恨，張再還而有述。 忽牽短而濫官，司惇史於藏室。 慚班子之繁麗，微馬生之簡實。 復通籍而延寵，陪帝扃之華密。 信儀鳳之所栖，乃絲文之自出。 歷五載而徘徊，猶官命之不改。 謝能飛於無翼，故同滯於有待。 晚加秩於戎章，乃□號之斯在。
That Eastern Pavilion's pure splendor—there the charge was weighty for wielding the brush. When Cai left once he left regret behind; when Zhang returned twice he had something to tell. Suddenly, though short in talent, I was wrongly given office and kept the solemn histories in the archive chamber. I was shamed before the Ban clan's ornate richness and fell short of Master Ma's plain truth. Again I entered the rolls and received extended favor, attending the emperor's inner gate in splendid secrecy. Truly where the ceremonial phoenix roosts—there silk writing issues of itself. For five years I lingered, yet the official appointment did not change. Xie could fly without wings; therefore I likewise stalled in waiting. Late I received rank in the military register—there □ title stood.

屬運道之將季，諒冠屨之無礙。 奄昇御於鼎湖，忽流哀於四海。 昔漢命之中微，皇統於是三絕。 暨孝昌之陵陂，亦繼□而禍結。 將小雅之詩廢，復三綱之道滅。 思跼蹐於時昏，獨沉吟於運閉。 遂退處於窮里，不外交於人世。 及數反於中興，驅時雄而電逝。 既籍取亂之權，方乘轉圓之勢。 俄隙開而守廢，遂冠冕之毀裂。 彼膏原而塗野，嗟衞肝與嵇血。
It fell when the age's way was nearing its end; I trusted that cap and shoes would not hinder me. Suddenly the emperor ascended at Ding Lake; suddenly grief flowed through the four seas. Formerly in Han's mid-decline the imperial line thrice ended. At the Xiao Chang tomb-slope disaster also followed □ and calamity knotted. The Odes of Lesser Ya were abandoned; again the way of the three bonds was extinguished. I brooded cramped in the age's darkness and alone sank in thought as fortune closed. Then I withdrew to a poor hamlet and did not mingle with the human world outside. When restoration returned several times, the heroes of the age drove like lightning and vanished. They already borrowed the power to seize disorder and were just then riding the momentum of a turning wheel. Soon the breach opened and defense was abandoned; then cap and robe were torn apart. There the plain was grease and the wilds were painted; alas for Wei Zhi's liver and Ji Kang's blood.

何古今之一揆，每治少而亂多。 盧遁身於東掖，荀窘迹於南羅。 時獲逃於□阜，仍竄宿於巖阿。 首丘急於明發，東路長其如何。 遽登舟而鼓柂，乃沿洛而汎河。 騖寸陰於不測，競征鳥於歸波。 時在所而放命，連百萬於山東。 何信都之巨猾，若封豕與大風。 肆吞噬於觜距，咸邑燼而野空。 徑黎陽之寇聚，迫崖壘之渢隆。 躁通川而鼎沸，矢交射於舟中。 備百罹於茲日，諒陳蔡之非窮。 乘虎口而獲濟，陵陽侯而迅往，得投憩於濮陽，實陶衞之舊壤。 望鄉村而佇立，曾不遙之河廣。 聞虜馬之夕嘶，見胡塵之晝上。
Why is ancient and modern one measure—each time order is brief and disorder abundant? Lu hid his body in the eastern side-gate; Xun cramped his tracks in the southern net. For a time I escaped to □ hill and still lurked and lodged in cliff caves. Longing for the home mound was urgent at dawn; the eastern road—how long would it be? Hastily I boarded a boat and beat the oar, then followed the Luo and floated the river. I raced the inch of shadow into the unknowable and competed with homeward birds on the returning waves. At the time they acted by whim wherever they were and linked a million men east of the mountains. What great villains of Xindu—like a penned boar and a great wind! They devoured at beak and claw; cities burned to ash and the wilds were empty. I passed the bandit muster at Liyang and pressed the cliff ramparts' roaring heights. The open river seethed like a cauldron; arrows crossed and shot into the boat. That day I endured a hundred calamities; truly the straits of Chen and Cai were not destitution. Riding the tiger's mouth I still crossed; passing the Lord of Yang I swiftly went on and found rest at Puyang—the old soil of Tao and Wei. Gazing at the village I stood and waited; the river's breadth was not far. I heard the barbarian horses neigh at evening and saw barbarian dust rise by day.

王略恢而廟勝，車徒發而雷響。 扇風師之猛氣，張天罼之層網。 裁一鼓而冰銷，俄氛祲之廓蕩。 昔蘧生之出奔，覩亡徵於亂政。 及季子之來反，乃君立而位定。 伊吾人之蕞爾，本無傒於衰盛。 忻草茅而偃伏，且優遊於辰慶。 復推斥於宦流，延光華於璽命。 甫聞內侍之忝，復奉優加之令。 何金紫之陸離，鬱貂玉之相映。
The royal plan was vast and the temple had victory; chariots and foot set out with thunder's roar. They fanned the wind-lord's fierce breath and spread heaven's net in layered mesh. At one drumstroke ice melted; soon the baleful air was cleared and scattered. Formerly when Qu Sheng fled abroad he saw the sign of ruin in disorderly government. When the younger son returned, then the lord was established and the throne was fixed. Alas for my slight person—I originally had no hope in decline or ascent. I rejoiced to lie low in thatched huts and for a time wandered at ease in the imperial celebration. Again I was pushed back into the stream of office and received the imperial seal's splendor. Just as I heard of the inner attendant's undeserved post, again I received the edict of special favor. What a glitter of gold and purple; sable and jade gleamed against each other.

時權定之云初，尚民心之易擾。 何建武之明傑，茂雄姿於天表。 忽靈命之有歸，藉親均而爭紹。 師出楚而飈發，旆陵江而雲矯。 闢閶闔之崢嶸，端冕旒於億兆。 神駕逝以流越，翠華飈而繚繞。 苟命舛而數違，雖功深而祚天。 時難忽然已及，網羅周其四張。 非五三之親暱，罕狥節於漢陽。 彼百僚之冠帶，咸北面於西王。 矧恩疏而任遠，固身存而義亡。 及宸居之反正，振天網於頹綱。 甄大義以明罰，虛半列於周行。 乃褫帶而來反，驅下澤於故鄉。
When power was first settled, the people's hearts were still easily disturbed. How brilliant was Jianwu, with heroic bearing above the heavens. Suddenly the numinous mandate had a destination; relying on kin ties they competed for succession. Armies left Chu like a gale; banners crossed the river like clouds bending. They opened the towering Bright Gate and set the crown and tassels straight before the hundred millions. The spirit carriage passed in flowing flight; the emerald canopy streamed and wound. If fate is crooked and fortune turns against you, though merit runs deep, heaven alone decides how long the throne may last. Hardship suddenly arrived; nets and snares closed on all four sides. Not kin like the Five Emperors and Three Kings—few died for principle at Hanyang. Those hundred officials in caps and sashes—all turned north to the Western King. How much more when favor was distant and trust far—surely body survived but principle perished. When the imperial seat returned to right rule, the heavenly net was shaken out from the collapsed cords. Great principle was sifted to make punishment clear; half the ranks in the court procession stood empty. Then I stripped my belt and returned, driving the lower marsh-cart to my old home.
60
探宿志以內求，撫身途而自計。 不詭遇以邀合，豈釣名以干世。 獨浩然而任己，同虛舟之不繫。 既未識其所以來，亦豈知其所以逝。 於是得喪同遣，忘懷自深。 遇物栖息，觸地山林。 雖因西浮之迹，何異東都之心。 願自託於魚鳥，永得性於飛沉。 庶保此以獲沒，不再罪於當今。
I sought my long-held purpose within and weighed my life's path for myself. I did not meet fortune by crooked means to win alliance; how could I fish for fame to meddle with the world? Alone I was vast and entrusted myself to my own way, like an empty boat with no mooring. Since I had not yet known whence I came, how could I know whither I would go? Then gain and loss were sent off alike, and forgetting lodged deep within. Where things were met I rested; wherever earth was touched there were hills and forests. Though my tracks drifted west like floating weed, what difference from the heart of one who hid in the Eastern Capital? I wish to cast my lot with fish and birds, forever at home in flight and in the depths. May this preserve me to a peaceful end, and keep me from offending the age I live in.

孝靜初，遭母憂，還鄉里。 徵為魏尹，將軍如故，以禫制未終，表辭。 朝議亦以為優，仍許其讓。 蕭衍求通和好，朝廷盛選行人，以諧兼散騎常侍，為聘使主。 諧至石頭，蕭衍遣其主客郎范胥當接。 諧問胥曰：「主客在郎官幾時？ 」胥答曰：「我本訓冑虎門，適復今任。 」諧言：「國子博士不應左轉為郎。 」胥答曰：「特為應接遠賓，故權兼耳。 」諧言：「屈己濟務，誠得事宜。 由我一介行人，令卿左轉。 」胥答曰：「自顧菲薄，不足對揚盛美，豈敢言屈。 」胥問曰：「今猶尚暖，北間當小寒於此？ 」諧答曰：「地居陰陽之正，寒暑適時，不知多少。 」胥曰：「所訪鄴下，豈是測影之地？ 」諧答曰：「皆是皇居帝里，相去不遠，可得統而言之。 」胥曰：「洛陽既稱盛美，何事遷鄴？ 」諧答曰：「不常厥邑，于茲五邦，王者無外，所在關河，復何所怪？ 」胥曰：「殷人否危，故遷相耿，貴朝何為而遷？ 」諧答：「聖人藏往知來，相時而動，何必俟於隆替？ 」胥曰：「金陵王氣兆於先代，黃旗紫蓋，本出東南，君臨萬邦，故宜在此。 」諧答曰：「帝王符命，豈得與中國比隆？ 紫蓋黃旗，終於入洛，無乃自害也？ 有口之說，乃是俳諧，亦何足道！ 」蕭衍親問諧曰：「魏朝人士，德行四科之徒凡有幾人？ 」諧對曰：「本朝多士，義等如林，文武賢才，布在列位，四科之美，非無其人，庸短造次，無以備啟。 」衍曰：「武王有亂臣十人，魏雖人物之盛，豈得頓如卿言？ 」諧曰：「愚謂周稱十人，本舉佐命，至於『濟濟多士』，實是文王之詩。 皇朝廊廟之才，足與周人有競。 」衍曰：「若爾，文足標異、武有冠絕者，便可指陳。 」諧曰：「大丞相勃海王秉文經武，左右皇極，畫一九州，懸衡四海。 錄尚書、汝陽王元叔昭、尚書令元世儁，宗室之秀，綰政朝端。 左僕射司馬子如、右僕射高隆之，並時譽民英，勠力匡輔。 侍中高岳、侍中孫騰，勳賢忠亮，宣讚王猷。 自餘才美不可具悉。 」衍曰：「故宜輔弼幼主，永固基業，深不可言。 」江南稱其才辯。
Early in Emperor Xiaojing's reign, Li Xie entered mourning for his mother and returned home. He was summoned to serve as Intendant of the Capital District, retaining his general's rank, but because his mourning period was not yet complete he memorialized to decline. The court found his refusal admirable and allowed him to stand aside. When Xiao Yan asked for peace and good relations, the court chose its envoys with care and appointed Li Xie concurrent Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and head of the embassy. Li Xie reached Stone City, where Xiao Yan sent his Master of Guests, Fan Xu, to receive him. Li Xie asked Fan Xu, "How long have you held the post of Master of Guests among the gentleman attendants? " Fan Xu answered, "I was trained at the Tiger Gate Academy and have only just taken up this present assignment. " Li Xie said, "An Erudite of the National University ought not be demoted to a gentleman attendant. " Fan Xu answered, "This is only to receive guests from afar, so I am temporarily holding the post. " Li Xie said, "To humble oneself for the sake of duty is indeed the right thing to do. Because of a mere envoy like me, you have been demoted. " Fan Xu answered, "I am too slight in talent to answer and proclaim such grandeur—how dare I speak of being humbled? " Fan Xu asked, "It is still warm now; must the north be a little colder than here? " Li Xie answered, "The land stands in the true balance of yin and yang, and cold and heat arrive in season—I do not know how much difference there is. " Fan Xu said, "The Ye of which you speak—is that truly a place for measuring the gnomon's shadow? " Li Xie answered, "They are all seats of emperors and imperial capitals, not far apart; one may speak of them together. " Fan Xu said, "If Luoyang was already praised as splendid, why move the capital to Ye? " Li Xie answered, "Not dwelling forever in one place—with five capitals to this point—the ruler knows no 'outside'; wherever stand the passes and rivers, what is there to wonder at? " Fan Xu said, "The Yin people were in peril and decline, so they moved to Xiang and Geng—why did your dynasty move its capital? " Li Xie answered, "The sage preserves the past and foreknows the future; he moves with the times—why must he wait for dynastic rise and fall? " Fan Xu said, "The royal aura of Jinling was foretold in earlier ages; the yellow banner and purple canopy arise in the southeast—to rule the myriad realms, the capital ought to be here. " Li Xie answered, "The mandate of a true emperor—how can it be compared in grandeur with the Central States? The purple canopy and yellow banner will in the end enter Luoyang—is that not cutting your own throat? Mere talk on everyone's lips is only wordplay—what is there worth saying! " Xiao Yan himself asked Li Xie, "Among the men of Wei, how many belong to the Four Categories of virtue and conduct? " Li Xie replied, "Our dynasty has many scholars, righteousness thick as a forest; civil and military worthies fill every post. There are indeed men who embody the Four Categories—but I am too crude and unprepared to report them all. " Xiao Yan said, "King Wu had ten ministers who brought order—though Wei is rich in talent, can it really match what you describe? " Li Xie said, "I take it that when Zhou speaks of ten men, it means those who aided the mandate; as for 'The many scholars, in full array,' that is in fact a poem of King Wen. The talents of our court are fully able to stand comparison with the men of Zhou. " Xiao Yan said, "If so, name those whose civil attainments are outstanding or whose martial prowess is unmatched. " Li Xie said, "The Grand Chancellor, Prince of Bohai, unites civil and military mastery, steadies the imperial throne, unifies governance across the Nine Provinces, and holds the scales over the Four Seas. Director of the Secretariat Prince of Ruyang Yuan Shuzhao and Director Yuan Shijun—outstanding scions of the imperial house who hold the reins of government at court. Left Vice Director Sima Ziru and Right Vice Director Gao Longzhi—both celebrated as the finest men of the age, laboring together to support the throne. Attendants-in-Chief Gao Yue and Sun Teng—meritorious, worthy, loyal, and upright, proclaiming and advancing the royal design. As for the rest, their talents and virtues cannot all be recounted. " Xiao Yan said, "So they ought to assist the young ruler and secure the foundation forever—profound beyond words. The lands south of the Yangzi praised his talent and eloquence.
62
使還，除大司農卿，加驃騎將軍，轉祕書監。 遇偏風廢頓。 武定二年卒，年四十九，時人悼惜之。 贈驃騎大將軍、衞尉卿、齊州刺史。 所著文集，別有集錄行於世。
On his return from the embassy, he was appointed Minister of Grand Agriculture, promoted to General of Flying Cavalry, and made Director of the Secretariat Library. He suffered a stroke that left half his body paralyzed. In the second year of Wuding he died at forty-nine, to the grief of all who knew him. He was posthumously honored as Grand General of Flying Cavalry, Minister of the Guard, and Governor of Qizhou. The collected works he authored circulated separately in a catalog of his writings.
63
長子嶽，武定末，司徒祭酒。
His eldest son Yue, at the end of the Wuding era, served as Libationer of the Minister of Education.
64
嶽弟庶，尚書南主客郎。
Yue's younger brother Shu served as Gentleman Master of Guests for the South in the Ministry of Works.
65
諧弟邕，字修穆。 幼而儁爽，有逸才。 著作佐郎、高陽王雍友。 凡所交遊皆倍年，儁秀才藻之美，為時所稱。 年二十五，卒。 贈鎮遠將軍、洛州刺史，諡曰文。
Li Xie's younger brother Yong, courtesy name Xiumu. From boyhood he was brilliant and free-spirited, with exceptional talent. He served as Associate Gentleman of the Editorial Office and as companion to Prince of Gaoyang, Yuan Yong. All his friends were twice his age, yet the brilliance of his talent and prose won praise throughout the age. He died at twenty-five. He was posthumously honored as General Who Subdues the Distance and Governor of Luozhou, with the posthumous title Wen.
66
史臣曰：邢巒以文武才策，當軍國之任，內參機揆，外寄折衝，其緯世之器歟？ 李平以高明幹略，効智於時，出入當官，功名克著，蓋贊務之英也。
The historian writes: Xing Luan, with civil and military talent and strategic counsel, bore the burdens of army and state—counseling within, repelling enemies without—is he not an instrument to order an age? Li Ping, with lofty clarity and practical wisdom, applied his intelligence to the times; in every office he held, merit and fame followed—surely a hero among those who sustain the state.
67
校勘記
Collation notes
68
河間鄚人也諸本「鄚」訛「鄭」，今據北史卷四三邢巒傳改。
"A man of Mo in Hejian commandery": in various editions "Mo" is erroneously written "Zheng"; the text is now emended according to the Beishi biography of Xing Luan (juan 43).
69
舉等進師討之諸本「舉」作「懸」，冊府卷三五三 〈四一九五頁〉 作「舉」。 按「舉」即指上文的「楊舉」，作「懸」無義，今據改。
"Yang Ju and the others advanced troops to attack them": in various editions "Ju" is written "Xuan"; Cefu juan 353 〈page 4195〉 reads "Ju." "Ju" refers to "Yang Ju" mentioned above; reading "Xuan" is meaningless; the text is now emended accordingly.
70
冠軍將軍魯方達固南安諸本「魯」作「曾」，通鑑卷一四六 〈四五四九頁〉 作「魯」。 按「魯方達」屢見卷八世宗紀正始二年、卷九八蕭衍傳，是這次戰事中梁朝重要將領。 梁書卷一０鄧元起傳中也幾次提到他，當時別無「曾方達」其人。 「曾」乃「魯」之訛，今據改。
"Champion General Lu Fangda fortified Nan'an": in various editions "Lu" is written "Zeng"; Zizhi Tongjian juan 146 〈page 4549〉 reads "Lu." "Lu Fangda" appears repeatedly in juan 8 (Basic Annals of Emperor Shizong), second year of Zhengshi, and juan 98 (biography of Xiao Yan); he was an important Liang general in this campaign. The Liangshu biography of Deng Yuanqi (juan 10) also mentions him several times; there was no person named "Zeng Fangda" at the time. "Zeng" is an error for "Lu"; the text is now emended accordingly.
71
蕭淵藻是裙屐少年諸本「裙屐」作「羣劇」，北史卷四三、通鑑卷一四六 〈四五五二頁〉 作「裙屐」。 按「羣劇」無義，今據改。
"Xiao Yuanzao was a silk-clad dandy of youth": in various editions "silk-clad dandy" is written "crowd play"; Beishi juan 43 and Zizhi Tongjian juan 146 〈page 4552〉 reads "silk-clad dandy." "Crowd play" is meaningless; the text is now emended accordingly.
72
便戮鄧元起諸本「起」作「超」。 按蕭淵藻殺鄧元起，事見南史卷五五鄧元起傳。 梁書卷一０鄧元起傳說元起「被收付州獄，於獄自縊」，微異，但死於淵藻之手的是鄧元起則一，「超」字訛，今改正。
"At once executed Deng Yuanqi": in various editions "Qi" is written "Chao." Xiao Yuanzao's killing of Deng Yuanqi is recorded in the Nanshi biography of Deng Yuanqi (juan 55). The Liangshu biography of Deng Yuanqi (juan 10) says Yuanqi "was arrested and handed over to the provincial prison, where he hanged himself in custody"—a slight difference—but that he died at Yuanzao's hands is the same; "Chao" is erroneous and is now corrected.
73
比建議之始通鑑卷一四六 〈四五五四頁〉 「比」下有「道遷」二字「議」作「義」。 按上二字當是通鑑所增，「議」疑當作「義」。
"At the beginning of the proposed plan": Zizhi Tongjian juan 146 〈page 4554〉 After "bi" there are the two characters "Dao Qian"; "yi" (議) is written "yi" (義). The two characters above were likely added by the Tongjian; "yi" (議) is suspected to read "yi" (義).
74
驍騎將軍相文玉等率眾一萬屯於孤山冊府卷三一三 〈四一九六頁〉 「相」作「桓」。 按卷八世宗紀正始三年七月丙寅稱「衍將桓和寇孤山，陷固城」，八月壬寅又稱「邢巒破蕭衍將桓和於孤山」。 卷九八蕭衍傳同，並不見所謂「相文玉」。 通鑑卷一四六 〈四五六三頁〉 也作「桓和屯孤山」，而此傳下文兩見「文玉」，通鑑都作「和」。 則司馬光所見魏書當作「桓文玉」，故認為「文玉」即「桓和」。 這裏「相」當是「桓」之訛，「文玉」或是和字。
"General of Valiant Cavalry Xiang Wenyu and others led ten thousand troops to encamp at Gushan": Cefu juan 313 〈page 4196〉 "Xiang" is written "Huan." According to juan 8 (Basic Annals of Emperor Shizong), third year of Zhengshi, seventh month, day bingyin, it reads "Yan's general Huan He raided Gushan and took Gucheng"; eighth month, day renyin, it again reads "Xing Luan defeated Xiao Yan's general Huan He at Gushan." Juan 98 (biography of Xiao Yan) agrees, and nowhere appears the supposed "Xiang Wenyu." Zizhi Tongjian juan 146 〈page 4563〉 Also reads "Huan He encamped at Gushan"; yet this biography twice mentions "Wenyu" below, and the Tongjian both times reads "He." Thus the Book of Wei as seen by Sima Guang should read "Huan Wenyu"; hence he identified "Wenyu" with "Huan He." Here "Xiang" is likely an error for "Huan"; "Wenyu" may be the character "He."
75
而懷恭等復於清南造城諸本「清」作「淮」，冊府卷三五三 〈四一九六頁〉 、通鑑卷一四六 〈四五六四頁〉 「淮」作「清」。 按宿豫城在泗水即清水旁，「淮」字訛，今據改。
"Huai Gong and the others again built a fortress south of Qing": in various editions "Qing" is written "Huai"; Cefu juan 353 〈page 4196〉 , Zizhi Tongjian juan 146 〈page 4564〉 "Huai" is written "Qing." Suyu city stood on the Si River—that is, beside the Qing River; "Huai" is erroneous, and the text is now emended accordingly.
76
非可抑為必勝諸本「勝」字闕，今據冊府卷四０四 〈四八０七頁〉 補。
"One cannot suppress them into assured victory": in various editions the character "sheng" is missing; it is now supplied according to Cefu juan 404 〈page 4807〉 supplied.
77
蕭密餘軍猶自在彼按「蕭密」即梁臨川王蕭宏，卷八世宗紀正始三年四月作「蕭容」，「密」「容」都是避元宏諱改。 參卷八校記[一二]。
"Xiao Mi's remaining troops were still there": "Xiao Mi" is the Liang Prince of Linchuan, Xiao Hong; juan 8 (Basic Annals of Emperor Shizong), third year of Zhengshi, fourth month reads "Xiao Rong"—both "Mi" and "Rong" are taboo-avoidance substitutions for Yuan Hong. See collation note [12] to juan 8.
78
喪元隸豎諸本「豎」訛「賢」，不可解，今據冊府卷四二八 〈五０九九頁〉 改。
"Sang Yuan's servant Shu": in various editions "Shu" is erroneously written "Xian," which is unintelligible; it is now emended according to Cefu juan 428 〈page 5099〉 Emended.
79
度公之在彼諸本此句作「兼云□公在彼」，不可解，今據冊府 〈同上卷頁〉 補改。
"When the Duke of Measure is there": various editions read "Moreover it says □ Duke is there," which is unintelligible; the text now follows the Cefu. 〈same fascicle, page〉 Supplemented and emended.
80
所製詩賦箴諫詠頌按「諫」非文體之名，疑是「誄」之訛。
"The poems, rhapsodies, admonitions, remonstrances, songs, and eulogies he composed": "remonstrance" is not a literary genre here and is likely a corruption of "dirge" (eulogy for the dead).
